papers.title: Summation-by-parts operators for general function spaces: Flux differencing, entropy stability, and accuracy
papers.abstract: Summation-by-parts (SBP) operators are a cornerstone of provably stable high-order methods for hyperbolic conservation laws. For nonlinear problems, the flux-differencing framework of Fisher and Carpenter combines such SBP operators with entropy-conservative two-point fluxes to obtain semi-discretizations that are conservative in the sense of Lax--Wendroff and discretely entropy-conservative or stable. So far, this framework has been developed exclusively for operators that are exact for polynomials. Function-space SBP (FSBP) operators lift this restriction by being exact on a general finite-dimensional function space that can be tailored to the problem at hand. In this work, we extend flux differencing to FSBP operators for general (potentially non-polynomial) function spaces. We prove that, whenever the operator has a diagonal norm and its function space contains the constants, the resulting semi-discretization is conservative in the sense of Lax--Wendroff, semi-discretely entropy-conservative within a single element, and entropy-stable across element interfaces. We also provide the first theoretical accuracy analysis of FSBP operators: We characterize their design order through an algebraic criterion on the underlying function space, prove that suitable non-polynomial spaces achieve the same design order as polynomial spaces of equal dimension, and show that the flux-differencing semi-discretization retains this order. Notably, the entropy-conservative two-point flux is reused unchanged; only the underlying function space differs from the polynomial case. Numerical experiments for the Burgers' equation and the compressible Euler equations in one and two dimensions confirm these properties.

papers.title: Denominators of Hodge integrals and Minkowski numbers
papers.abstract: We prove that the least common denominator of all genus $g$ Hodge integrals is the Minkowski number $T_{2g}$ or, equivalently, the Bhargava factorial $(2g+1)!_{\mathbb{P}}$ associated to the set of primes $\mathbb{P}\subset\mathbb{N}$. As a corollary, we prove a conjecture of Liu-Xu on the multiplicity of $3$ in the least common denominators of certain descendant integrals, and generalise their result on a conjecture of Itzykson-Zuber to Hodge integrals with $λ$ classes. Namely, the order of the automorphism group of any pointed stable curve of genus $g'\le g$ divides the least common denominator of all genus $g$ Hodge integrals. We also comment on the use of generative AI via IMProofBench, which played a fruitful part in the development of this (entirely human-written) paper.

papers.title: Global well-posedness for the modified dispersion-generalized Benjamin-Ono equations
papers.abstract: In this short note, we prove the global well-posedness of the modified dispersion-generalized Benjamin-Ono equation with dispersion $1<α<2$, $$\partial_t u + D^α\partial_x u + u^2\partial_x u=0,$$ over the Sobolev space $H^s(\mathbb{R})$, for any regularity $s$ greater or equal than the sharp analytic well-posedness regularity. As a byproduct, we also derive nonlinear smoothing estimates and give a simple proof of local well-posedness.

papers.title: Syzygy and Adjoint Matroids
papers.abstract: We give a matroid-theoretic analogue of Gaussian elimination and use it to construct, for every matroid M, the syzygy matroid Syz(M) on the collection of circuits of M. Dualizing the construction yields the combinatorial adjoint Adj(M) on the collection of maximal proper flats of M, and the two are related by Adj(M) \simeq Syz(M*). Neither construction depends on a realization. We determine Syz(M) when M is U_{k,k+3} or the Vamos matroid V_{8}. We also show that Adj(M) is an adjoint of M when M has rank 3. When M has rank 4 and V_{8} is a restriction of M, Adj(M) has rank 3 and is not an adjoint of M.

papers.title: Quantum field theory and four-manifolds: Perspectives from physics and geometry
papers.abstract: These lecture notes are based on lecture series by the authors for the Summer School 2025 on ``Physical mathematics of quantum field theory" at the University of Massachusetts Amherst organized by Owen Gwilliam, Chris Elliott, and Matteo Lotito. The lectures centred around algebraic structures arising from twists of supersymmetric quantum field theories, correlation functions of topologically twisted supersymmetric gauge theories, and their mathematical counterparts as intersection-theoretic invariants associated to moduli spaces of instantons, semistable sheaves, or Higgs sheaves on four-manifolds or complex projective surfaces.

papers.title: Generalized Images for Brownian First Passage to Monomial Boundaries
papers.abstract: We study the first passage of Brownian motion to a monomial moving boundary. For every integer degree at least two, we construct a time-independent signed image measure whose heat potential is the killed Brownian transition density on a nonzero interval of the natural Brownian time scale. The image density is determined by a second-kind Volterra equation in the image coordinate, not by the classical Volterra equations in time for the hitting density. Its kernel is an explicit Wright function, and the first-passage density is recovered afterwards from the boundary flux. Exponential bounds establish convergence, while a beta-moment transform connects the Wright kernel with the finite-order differential hierarchy previously obtained from transported moving zeros. A cubic numerical experiment independently checks the resulting density against simulated Brownian paths.

papers.title: Cographs in chordal graphs
papers.abstract: For a graph $G$, let $\text{cg}(G)$ be the maximum $k\in \mathbb N$ for which $G$ contains a $k$-vertex cograph as an induced subgraph. The Erdős-Hajnal conjecture asserts that for every proper hereditary graph class $\mathcal{G}$, there exists $γ\in(0,1]$ such that every $n$-vertex graph $G\in\mathcal{G}$ satisfies $\text{cg}(G)\geq n^γ$. This is still open; however, for some hereditary classes, one may guarantee much stronger bounds. For instance, every chordal graph $G$ on $n\geq 2$ vertices satisfies $\text{cg}(G)\geq n/(2\log n)$. Paul Seymour asked whether this bound is optimal up to a constant factor. We answer this affirmatively, even for interval graphs: For every integer $n\geq 2$, we construct an $n$-vertex interval graph $G$ with $\text{cg}(G)<64n/\log n$.

papers.title: Continuous-time analysis and algorithms for linear and convex quadratic programs via exactly solvable differential inclusions
papers.abstract: Linear and convex quadratic programs are fundamental problems in optimization. While many methods have been developed for solving these programs in large-scale applications, to our knowledge none have attempted to solve their continuous-time gradient flow, a differential inclusion, in full generality without assumptions beyond feasibility. Recent work solved the gradient flows in two special cases, basis pursuit and the lasso, and obtained competitive algorithms. Motivated by these results, we solve the general case exactly. Using the minimal selection principle for monotone differential inclusions, we show that the trajectory of the gradient flow consists of finitely many pieces, each obtained from one nonnegative least-squares problem. Its final piece yields an optimal solution or a certificate of unboundedness. This analysis leads to two algorithms. The first algorithm is exact, terminates after finitely many steps, and applies to linear programs and projections onto polyhedra. The second algorithm, which we call minimal selection descent, discretizes the gradient flow for general convex quadratic programs. Its iterates converge to an optimal solution when one exists and otherwise certify unboundedness. We apply both algorithms to a positivity-preserving limiter for a discontinuous Galerkin scheme and to optimal control problems for the Poisson and heat equations. In the limiter, the first algorithm conserves the total mass more accurately than the state-of-the-art Douglas--Rachford splitting method. On the control problems, minimal selection descent reaches the optimal value to machine precision and is competitive in time with commercial and open-source solvers.

papers.title: On Borodin-Gorin presentation of Heckman-Opdam $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ hypergeometric function
papers.abstract: We prove that Borodin-Gorin presentation for Heckman-Opdam $\mathfrak{gl}_n$ hypergeometric function by interlacing integrals is equivalent to two other integral presentations studied in arXiv:2508.18864. We also consider related Baxter operators and the corresponding limiting procedure from the Ruijsenaars hyperbolic model.

papers.title: Structure-Preserving Dimension Reduction and Surrogates for Partially Linear Bayesian Inverse Problems
papers.abstract: Many Bayesian inverse problems are characterized by two parameter vectors with distinct roles. A medium property, operator coefficient, or geometry block enters the forward model nonlinearly, whereas a volumetric, initial condition, or boundary condition source enters linearly. General-purpose nonlinear surrogates must relearn this known source dependence from data and may not preserve the correct source scaling outside the training regime. We introduce a structure-preserving partially linear (SPPL) framework that constructs separate reduced spaces for outputs, (linearly appearing) sources, and (nonlinearly appearing) medium variables and represents the reduced forward map as an affine function of the retained source coordinates, with coefficients that depend on the medium variables. Here, "affine" refers to the retained, mean-centered source coordinates: the physical forward map remains linear in the source, while the affine offset is induced by the source-prior mean and vanishes when that mean is zero. The analysis first identifies the optimal blockwise ridge approximation and then derives the optimal affine-in-source approximation under independent medium and source priors. A direct decomposition of the forward error into output, source, medium, and surrogate contributions yields blockwise spectral criteria and prior-predictive expected-KL control. For a Gaussian source prior, the optimal affine-in-source approximation coincides with the optimal blockwise ridge approximation. In a coseismic numerical example, a three-model controlled ablation on common block-reduced coordinates separates the effects of coefficient-matrix supervision and structure-preserving affine-in-source parameterization. Reduced-space surrogate MCMC provides orders-of-magnitude online acceleration relative to high-fidelity posterior sampling.

papers.title: Matrix-Free Local Multigrid for $C^1$ Hermite Discretizations on GPUs
papers.abstract: I present a matrix-free local multigrid method for $C^1$ tensor-product Hermite discretizations on adaptively refined Cartesian meshes, using the clamped biharmonic problem as the model problem. Extending a cell-wise primal-dual formulation to Hermite elements, I enforce continuity through a constraint operator that is never formed. At refinement edges, geometric prolongation supplies both the trace and its normal derivative, so the local V-cycle needs no edge operator and no hanging-node machinery. For the cubic element, an even-odd decomposition based on the signed reflection symmetry of the Hermite basis, applied along two axes, splits the element matrix into four dense $16\times16$ blocks and reaches 85% of peak memory bandwidth. Chebyshev-Jacobi and vertex-patch smoothers both preserve conformity by construction. In three dimensions on one NVIDIA A100 in double precision, conjugate gradients preconditioned by the Chebyshev-Jacobi V-cycle need five or six iterations on uniform meshes and solve at up to 4.23 million cells per second. On locally refined meshes the count rises to at most sixteen, ordered by the fraction of cells on a refinement edge and nearly equal for both smoothers.

papers.title: Automorphisms of Twisted Chevalley Groups over Commutative Rings
papers.abstract: We classify all abstract automorphisms of the elementary and full twisted Chevalley groups of types ${}^2A_\ell$ ($\ell\geq3$), ${}^2D_\ell$ ($\ell\geq4$), ${}^2E_6$, and ${}^3D_4$ over arbitrary commutative rings, for every invariant isogeny type. The coefficient automorphism $θ$ has order dividing that of the diagram automorphism. We assume that $2$ is invertible and, for triality, that $3$ is invertible as well. Three features distinguish the answer from the usual inner--diagonal and coefficient decomposition. The elementary groups of types ${}^2A_3$ and ${}^2A_4$ admit an additive family of exceptional automorphisms supported at $θ$-fixed maximal ideals with residue field $\mathbb F_3$. In type ${}^2D_4$, diagram automorphisms may vary on idempotent components, subject to compatibility with the involution and the isogeny lattice. In triality, the coefficient automorphisms preserve the trace operator $r\mapsto r+θ(r)+θ^2(r)$ but need not commute with $θ$. We determine which elementary automorphisms extend to the full groups and describe the remaining central factors. A nonzero exceptional unitary factor extends precisely in the simply connected type ${}^2A_3$, giving a classification for the hyperbolic group $\operatorname{SU}_4(R,θ;Q_4)$. The proof glues uniquely determined normalization data for a finite root frame and then recovers the coefficient action from root-subgroup relations.

papers.title: Dynamic Active Fleet Sizing of Heterogeneous UAV Relays for Post-Disaster Communication Networks
papers.abstract: Uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) communication systems are increasingly used to provide temporary connectivity when ground communication infrastructure is damaged by disasters such as hurricanes and wildfires. However, the amount of aerial support required changes as ground networks recover and communication demand evolves. We focus on dynamically adjusting the number and allocation of actively deployed UAVs within a fixed available fleet. We develop a model predictive control (MPC) framework for dynamic fleet sizing of heterogeneous UAV relays during post-disaster communication recovery. The framework accounts for communication demand, ground network recovery, heterogeneous UAV operation, UAV energy availability, and backhaul capacity, which limits how much relayed traffic can be transmitted to the external communication network. The resulting formulation is a convex quadratic program that supports efficient online fleet sizing and deployment decisions. We evaluate the framework using seven historical disaster recovery case studies based on Federal Communications Commission reports, together with four backhaul scenarios and sensitivity analyses. Results show that required active UAV fleet size varies considerably throughout recovery, while backhaul capacity and fleet composition affect communication performance, highlighting the value of adapting active fleet size over time.

papers.title: Covering lemmas associated to maximal operators of weak type
papers.abstract: Building on the work of A. Córdoba and R. Fefferman, we provide a necessary and sufficient covering condition on a basis $\mathcal{B}$ on a separable metric space $X$ with a Borel measure $μ$ so that the associated \mbox{geometric} maximal operator $M_\mathcal{B}$ satisfies for all $α> 0$ the weak type estimate $$μ\left(\left\{x \in X : M_\mathcal{B}f(x) > α\right\}\right) \leq \int_{X}Φ\left( γ_\mathcal{B} \left|\frac{f}α\right|\right)\,dμ\;,$$ where $Φ: [0, \infty) \rightarrow [0, \infty)$ is an everywhere finite Young's function.

papers.title: Scattering of plane waves and a modified Pompeiu criterion
papers.abstract: In this paper we prove that plane waves always scatter from bounded, strictly convex planar inhomogeneities with constant material parameters. Our approach involves the introduction of a modified Pompeiu property, whose failure corresponds to the vanishing of the Fourier transform of the indicator function of the inhomogeneity on a complexified circle not centered at the origin. We then show that such vanishing is impossible for bounded, strictly convex planar sets.

papers.title: Finite time implosions of the multidimensional compressible Euler equations with a finite far-field cutoff
papers.abstract: We study the problem of finite time singularities in the isentropic compressible Euler equations in multiple dimensions with radial symmetry. Our initial data consists of the radially symmetric Kidder self-similar implosion with a continuous constant density cutoff. Motivated by our recent work on the one-dimensional problem, we present high-resolution radially symmetric adaptive mesh refinement simulations that when combined with asymptotic similarity solution analysis present a full picture of the ensuing dynamics of the implosion. From the cutoff point in the initial data, an expanding wave emerges. The endpoints of the wave follow the "imploding" and "exploding" characteristic speeds associated with the system of hyperbolic conservation laws. This wave has much more complex structure than the exact non-centered rarefaction wave that emerges in the one-dimensional problem. As in the one-dimensional case, the inner Kidder solution is swallowed up by the expanding wave as time approaches the singularity time. However, unlike the one-dimensional case, a blowup occurs along the point where the `imploding' side of the expanding wave attaches to the Kidder solution. This composite blowup has an asymptotic self-similar form that has an interpretation in terms of the Gurderley-type self-similarity structure. The numerical method for the PDE necessitates a Lagrangian scheme to avoid the numerical diffusion inherent in Eulerian methods. We use a leapfrog method coupled to recursive refinement of the mesh near the blowup, which allows for very high resolution simulations, resolving many orders of magnitude of the self-similar blowup. Consistent with prior rigorous results for these equations, the blowup does not involve mass concentration and exhibits a critical $L^p$ space for the concentration of the density, depending on the dimension of space.

papers.title: Simultaneous popular polynomial differences in higher dimensions
papers.abstract: We extend the simultaneous popular polynomial difference theorem of Conlon, Dong, and the author to polynomial shifts along prescribed directions in $\mathbb{F}_p^D$. Let $P_1,\ldots,P_k\in\mathbb{Z}[t]$ be linearly independent polynomials with zero constant terms, and let $v_1,\ldots,v_k\in\mathbb{Z}^D\setminus\{0\}$. We show that, for every $\varepsilon>0$, every sufficiently large prime $p$, and every $A\subseteq\mathbb{F}_p^D$ of density $α$, there exists a nonzero $d\in\mathbb{F}_p$ such that \[ \mathbb{E}_{\underline{x}\in\mathbb{F}_p^D} \mathbf{1}_A(\underline{x}) \prod_{\substack{1\leq i\leq k\\ ω_i=1}} \mathbf{1}_A\bigl(\underline{x}+P_i(d)v_i\bigr) \geq α^{\,1+\sum_{i=1}^kω_i}-\varepsilon \] simultaneously for every $ω\in\{0,1\}^k$. The main new ingredient is a directional arithmetic regularity decomposition adapted to mixed directional box norms.

papers.title: A note on functional non-central limit theorem for periodic regime-switching stable-like processes
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish a functional non-central limit theorem for regime-switching stable-like processes with periodic coefficients. Our approach relies on stochastic analysis methods, in particular semimartingale characteristics, combined with the ergodic theory of Markov processes. If the set on which the order function achieves its minimum value $\underlineα$ has positive Lebesgue measure, then the limit is a rotationally invariant $\underlineα$-stable Lévy process. Otherwise, the limit is the zero process.

papers.title: Optimal CLT error bounds in the second order Wasserstein metric via Stein's method for weakly dependent sequences
papers.abstract: We use Stein's method to prove general upper bounds on the second order Wasserstein distance in the CLT for general dependent partial sums $S_N=X_1+\ldots +X_N$. Then we use these estimates to provide optimal $O(N^{-1/2})$ rates for a variety of chaotic dynamical systems and $φ$- and $ψ$-mixing sequences. Our results for $ψ$-mixing sequences are obtained under the fourth moment condition, which matches the best known results in the iid case. This is the first time that optimal CLT rates of any kind are obtained for unbounded weakly stationary variables under general mixing conditions. We then apply this result and obtain optimal CLT rates $O\left((\text{Var}(S_N))^{-1/2}\right)$ for non-stationary $ψ$-mixing sequences without any growth rates on $\text{Var}(S_N)$. We also obtain close to optimal CLT rates for nonconventional sums and some classes of random dynamical systems with non-uniform decay of correlations

papers.title: Partial Breakdown of Integrability in Nearly Integrable Systems
papers.abstract: We study the persistence of integrable structures in real-analytic nearly integrable systems under perturbations that may destroy some, but not all, of these structures. Specifically, we establish upper bounds on the numbers of real-analytic first integrals -- quantities conserved by the motion -- and commuting vector fields -- infinitesimal generators of continuous symmetries -- that can persist under the perturbation. These bounds are expressed in terms of Melnikov-type functions, which quantify the breakdown of the corresponding integrable structures. Unlike classical Melnikov theory, our conditions occur even in the absence of zeros of the Melnikov functions, so they do not necessarily imply the existence of homoclinic tangles. We give a geometric interpretation of these conditions in the context of the Arnold diffusion problem, showing that they imply micro-diffusion. We also obtain a criterion for higher-dimensional nearly integrable systems in which the dimension of the span of the Melnikov vectors restricts the numbers of possible first integrals and commuting vector fields. This shows that the geometry of the Melnikov vectors provides a new mechanism for detecting the breakdown of integrability. We give several applications to integrable Hamiltonian systems subject to forcing and dissipation.

papers.title: A unified variational framework for augmented Lagrangian preconditioning of saddle point systems: applications to mixed-dimensional and fictitious domain methods
papers.abstract: We present a general framework to derive augmented Lagrangian preconditioners for saddle point systems arising from mixed finite element discretizations. Our approach is based on augmenting the variational formulation at the continuous level prior to discretization, providing a unified strategy for designing efficient preconditioners that are robust under mesh refinement for a broad class of problems leading to symmetric saddle point systems. The robustness of the proposed preconditioners is established through a detailed spectral analysis. This framework is applied to different model problems, focusing on mixed-dimensional and fictitious domain formulations involving Lagrange multipliers, with some configurations featuring large coefficient jumps. Extensive numerical experiments on different test cases and geometries are presented, validating the effectiveness and robustness of our preconditioners when used in conjunction with flexible GMRES.

papers.title: The Porous Medium Equation and Convexity
papers.abstract: We show that root convexity of the pressure is preserved by the porous medium equation if the initial data is root convex, positive, smooth, bounded below by a quadratic function and has bounded Laplacian. This complements a result of Daskalopoulos-Hamilton-Lee on root concavity of pressure.

papers.title: Relative Hitchin fibrations and endoscopy for Unitary Friedberg--Jacquet varieties
papers.abstract: We prove a relative fundamental lemma for the unitary symmetric variety $GL_n(k')\backslash U_{2n}$, proving a conjecture of Leslie, Xiao, and Zhang. Our proof reduces to the Lie algebra and argues over function fields in positive characteristic, using methods from Ngo-Laumon and Ngo. In particular, we reinterpret orbital integrals in terms of the cohomology of relative affine Springer fibers and globalize this using unitary versions of Hitchin moduli spaces for symmetric pairs via a product formula. As the main global input, we prove a matching of perverse sheaves between relative Hitchin moduli spaces and their corresponding endoscopic variants.

papers.title: Permutation classes need not have proper growth rates
papers.abstract: By the Marcus-Tardos Theorem (formerly the Stanley-Wilf Conjecture), every permutation class other than the class of all permutations has a finite upper growth rate, meaning that the $n$th root of the number of permutations of length $n$ in the class has a finite limit superior. It has long been conjectured that this limit superior is in fact always a proper limit. We disprove this by constructing a permutation class whose upper and lower growth rates differ. The construction uses grid classes with cubic row-column graphs of increasing girth, obtained from Haar graphs of finite 2-groups. The corresponding hereditary property of ordered graphs also disproves an analogous 2006 conjecture of Balogh, Bollobás, and Morris. Along the way, we show that every proper permutation class with a D-finite generating function has a proper growth rate. We also establish refined enumerative bounds for grid classes, which lead to a short proof of Albert and Vatter's generalization of Bevan's Theorem on the growth rates of grid classes.

papers.title: Asymptotical results on the automorphism groups of canonical double cover of graphs
papers.abstract: The canonical double cover $BX$ of a graph $X$ is the direct product $X\times K_2$. A graph $X$ is stable if every automorphism of $BX$ is induced by automorphisms of $X$ and $K_2$, and unstable otherwise. We prove several asymptotic results on stable and unstable graphs. In particular, we show that the automorphism group of the canonical double cover of almost every graph has order $2$, and consequently that almost all graphs are stable. We also prove that the dominant sources of instability are having twins and being disconnected, in that order, and that graphs arising from a known construction are the next step in this hierarchy.

papers.title: Isogenies of Oriented Elliptic Curves
papers.abstract: We construct and describe the moduli stack $\mathrm{Isog}$ of isogenies between oriented elliptic curves. We show that $\mathrm{Isog}$ is a spectral Deligne-Mumford stack and a relative spectral algebraic space over $\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{ell}}^{\mathrm{or}}$, and give a fiber product decomposition of $\mathrm{Isog}$ corresponding to a connected-étale factorization on oriented elliptic curves. In the process of proving these results, we construct a theory of duality and quotients for spectral abelian varieties, prove a higher-algebraic version of Nakayama's lemma, and lift the rigidity theorem for morphisms of elliptic curves to the setting of spectral algebraic geometry.

papers.title: Source integrability and the frontier $α=\tfrac12$ in time-fractional diffusion
papers.abstract: Let $Ω\subset\mathbb{R}^{d}$ be a bounded Lipschitz domain, let $α\in(0,1)$, and let $\partial_{t}^α$ denote the Caputo derivative. For $\partial_{t}^αu-\nabla\cdot\bigl(A(x)\nabla u\bigr)=f$ with homogeneous Dirichlet condition and initial datum $g\in L^{2}(Ω)$, we identify which of the thresholds appearing in the energy method belong to the method and which to the equation. We compare $f\in L^{2}\bigl((0,T);L^{2}(Ω)\bigr)$ and $f\in L^{r}\bigl((0,T);L^{2}(Ω)\bigr)$ with $r>2/α$; in the subdiffusive range the second implies the first and not conversely. Existence is not at issue and we claim none of it: it is known, for both hypotheses and under weaker ones, from the work of Zacher. What we determine is the exact set of exponents each route admits and what the exponents left outside it cost. Under the weaker hypothesis the construction below reaches $α\in(\frac12,1)$, under the stronger one every $α\in(0,1)$, and in both cases the solution lies in $L^{\infty}\bigl((0,T);L^{2}(Ω)\bigr)$, by the mode representation and not by the energy route, which yields no such bound under the weaker hypothesis. The restriction $α>\frac12$ comes from the compactness criterion, whose admissible exponents form $[1,2α)$; the exponent $r>2/α$ is exactly what the Grönwall step consumes. A concentrating family shows that nothing weaker suffices along that route, and the mode representation lowers the requirement to $1/α$. The frontier $α=\frac12$ belongs to the equation: for every $α\in(0,\frac12]$ there is $f\in L^{2}\bigl((0,T);L^{2}(Ω)\bigr)$ whose weak solution leaves $L^{\infty}\bigl((0,T);L^{2}(Ω)\bigr)$. Uniqueness and Hadamard well-posedness follow.

papers.title: The longest increasing subsequences of Luce permutations and permutons
papers.abstract: We investigate the longest increasing subsequences (LIS) of random permutations distributed under the Luce model with weights $θ_1^{(n)} \ge \ldots \ge θ_n^{(n)}$. Our first main result provides a general formula for the growth rate of the LIS. For example, we get that the LIS of Luce permutations with Sukhatme weights $θ_k^{(n)} = n-k+1$ grows like $\sqrt{n}$. We also give simple conditions for the LIS to be of order $n^β$, for any given $β\in[1/2,1)$. Our second main result states that, if the weights are of the form $θ_k^{(n)} = f\big( (k-1)/n \big)$ for a sufficiently regular function $f$, then the LIS divided by $2\sqrt{n}$ converges in probability to a constant $K(f)$ described by a variational problem. Throughout, we make extensive use of coupling techniques; in particular, to prove our second main result, we argue that Luce random permutations behave similarly to random permutations sampled from the ``Luce permuton''.

papers.title: Simple finite-dimensional binary Lie superalgebras
papers.abstract: We prove that every complex finite-dimensional simple binary Lie superalgebra with non-zero odd part is either a simple Lie superalgebra, and hence is one of the superalgebras of Kac's list, or the two-dimensional non-Lie superalgebra $B_2$. This confirms the Grishkov--Shestakov conjecture and, together with the theorems of Grishkov and Filippov on simple binary Lie algebras, gives the answer to Shestakov's question from the Dniester Notebook (Problem 3.100(d)) over the field of complex numbers.

papers.title: A Transformer-based Approach for Real-time Multi-agent Path Planning with Varying Initial/Final Conditions
papers.abstract: We address the problem of real-time multi-agent path planning under prescribed initial and final configurations, formulated as a high-dimensional optimal control problem subject to inter-agent collision avoidance and obstacle constraints. Classical solvers based on the Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman equation or Pontryagin's maximum principle (PMP) become computationally intractable as the number of agents grows, due to the curse of dimensionality and the non-convexity introduced by interaction constraints. We propose OCFormer, a transformer-based neural network that parameterizes the inverse of a coordinate transformation mapping a simple, analytically tractable latent space, in which agents evolve independently under a decoupled Hamiltonian, to the physical space of the coupled, interacting system. The model is trained by minimizing a physics-informed loss comprising the Hamiltonian ODE residual from the PMP and a boundary matching term, without requiring pre-computed trajectory data. The self-attention mechanism endows OCFormer with permutation equivariance over agents, a structural symmetry that prior symplectic network approaches do not natively enforce. When trained on a distribution of boundary conditions, the amortized OCFormer produces near-optimal trajectories for unseen initial and final configurations in a single forward pass ($\sim$220ms), enabling real-time inference without retraining. We further introduce a lightweight transfer learning framework that adapts a pretrained OCFormer to out-of-distribution perturbations in seconds via L-BFGS fine-tuning. Numerical experiments on two- and three-dimensional multi-agent navigation with up to 128 agents demonstrate the scalability and efficiency of the proposed approach.

papers.title: Robust topology optimization of isogeometric Kirchhoff--Love shells by the Speed Method
papers.abstract: This paper presents a framework for robust topology optimization of Kirchhoff-Love (KL) multi-patch shells using isogeometric analysis and non-matching meshes and provides a CAD-compatible method. The material distribution is optimized via a NURBS-based level set method, enabling accurate boundary representation and seamless export to standard CAD/CAM workflows. The shape derivative is computed using the speed method, yielding a volume-based formulation that avoids boundary approximations and aligns with the isogeometric principle of coarse, high-order discretizations. This eliminates the need for local refinement, adaptive quadrature, or trimming as the descent direction for the compliance and volume objectives are obtained through a biharmonic equation. The framework is extended to robust optimization under uncertainty, accounting for stochastic loading and material properties via Monte Carlo sampling and Gaussian Random Fields. Numerical examples demonstrate the method's efficiency and robustness across single- and multi-patch shells, reproducing literature results with fewer elements than traditional FEM or refined IGA approaches. The developed methods and tools can be directly extended to problems involving stress-based optimization and risk-averse metrics. The numerical implementations are open-source and available on GitHub.

papers.title: The symplectic leaves of the affine Poisson $C^\infty$-scheme associated with a singular subalgebroid
papers.abstract: Every singular subalgebroid, and in particular every singular foliation $\mathscr{G}$, determines a universal Poisson $C^\infty$-scheme $\mathrm{Spec}(\mathcal{F}(\mathscr{G}))$, which is the analogue of the linear Poisson structure on the dual of a Lie algebroid. We show that the underlying space $X_{\mathcal{F}(\mathscr{G})}$ of $\mathrm{Spec}(\mathcal{F}(\mathscr{G}))$ decomposes as a disjoint union of symplectic manifolds. Furthermore, we extend the Helffer-Nourrigat cone to a singular subalgebroid and show that it is an embedded Poisson $C^\infty$-subscheme of $\mathrm{Spec}(\mathcal{F}(\mathscr{G}))$.

papers.title: The Serrin exponent for Lane-Emden inequalities driven by sums of fractional p-Laplacians
papers.abstract: We study positive weak super-solutions of the Lane-Emden inequality $\mathcal{L}u := \sum_{i=1}^{n}(-Δ_{p_i})^{s_i}u \ge u^q$ in $\mathbb{R}^N$, where each $(-Δ_{p_i})^{s_i}$ is a fractional $p_i$-Laplacian of order $s_i\in(0,1]$ and exponent $p_i\in(1,\infty)$, and $\max_i s_ip_i<N$. Let $κ_i := (N-s_ip_i)/(p_i-1)$ be the decay exponent of the fundamental solution of the $i$-th operator, and let $\overlineκ := \max_iκ_i$. We show that the Serrin exponent of $\mathcal{L}$ is $\mathfrak{q}_{\mathcal{L}} = N/\overlineκ$. More precisely, for $0<q<\mathfrak{q}_{\mathcal{L}}$ the only non-negative continuous weak super-solution is $u\equiv 0$, while for every $q>\mathfrak{q}_{\mathcal{L}}$ we construct explicit positive weak super-solutions of the form $A(λ+|x|)^{-κ}$. In other words, the Serrin exponent of the sum is the smallest of the Serrin exponents $N/κ_i$ of the single operators, that is, the one of the operator whose fundamental solution decays fastest. No structural assumption relating the different operators is needed. The endpoint $q=\mathfrak{q}_{\mathcal{L}}$ is left open. The local order $s_i=1$ is treated together with the nonlocal orders, and all the arguments are carried out in the weak setting.

papers.title: New criteria for upper bounds on the number of limit cycles in Liénard systems
papers.abstract: We study upper bounds for isolated periodic orbits of generalized Liénard systems on a single potential well. Common-curvature and common-intercept conditions yield uniqueness and hyperbolicity, while a convex--concave condition on the potential-profile slopes gives an upper bound of two. The statements allow finite unequal potential endpoints; appropriate versions also admit degenerate restoring forces and reduced regularity. We prove a uniqueness extension across slope interfaces, a quantitative joint weak-damping criterion, and a compensation criterion controlled by two derivatives. A separate response comparison at neutral cycles, combined with a connected parameter-family argument, gives a coefficient criterion for a two-cycle bound. Applications include classical quartic systems, negative-parameter and positive-parameter Selkov systems, a uniqueness conjecture for arbitrary-degree polynomial systems, and explicit smooth and nonsmooth examples. Existence is proved separately whenever an exact count is asserted. Restrictions to a potential well, a parameter region, or a compact width interval are retained throughout.

papers.title: Injectivity and continuity of the intersection form in infinite type
papers.abstract: We study two fundamental properties of the intersection pairing between geodesic currents on infinite-type surfaces which are classical in the finite-type closed setting: injectivity of the marked length spectrum and continuity of the intersection form. We show that geodesic currents on infinite-type surfaces of the first kind are determined by their intersection numbers with closed curves, extending Otal's marked length spectrum rigidity argument from finite-type to infinite-type surfaces. In contrast, we prove that the intersection pairing is not continuous in general for the natural topologies by constructing explicit counterexamples. We then prove sufficient criteria for continuity of intersection numbers for infinite-type surfaces.

papers.title: A remoteness formula for generalized Wythoff games
papers.abstract: Smith's remoteness function records how long an impartial game lasts when the winner wins as quickly as possible and the loser delays defeat. For the generalized Wythoff game $\mathrm{WYT}(a,b)$, in which two positive integer parameters $a$ and $b$ determine which simultaneous removals from the two piles are allowed, we give a formula for the remoteness of every position, building on the known values at losing positions. The formula depends on two indices: a local index determined by the coordinates of the losing positions in a window of length $b$ ending at the smaller pile, and the integer part of the pile difference divided by $a$. When $b=1$, complementary Beatty sequences make the local index explicit, which gives an explicit formula for $\mathrm{WYT}(a,1)$, including classical Wythoff's game. We also show that if each attempted move in a finite impartial game independently fails with a fixed probability and passes the turn, the probability that the player to move wins under optimal play is an explicit exponential function of remoteness. For every success probability strictly between $0$ and $1$, the optimal attempts are exactly the moves that reduce remoteness by one.

papers.title: Reflections on Trusting Lean
papers.abstract: It is known, by works of Werner and Carneiro, that the type theory of Lean (and indeed of CIC plus a version of choice) is equiconsistent with ZFC plus "there are infinitely many strongly inaccessible cardinals". We prove a finer connection between these two formal systems; namely, given any formula in the language of second order arithmetic, that formula is provable in the aforementioned extension of ZFC if and only if the same formula, when viewed as a type in Lean, is inhabited.
papers.comments: This work has been presented at ICMS 2026 on 23 July 2026

papers.title: Energy-rate equidistribution for adaptive SSAV--BDF2 integration of gradient flows
papers.abstract: We develop an adaptive time-stepping strategy for scalar auxiliary variable (SAV) schemes combined with variable-step BDF2 discretization for gradient flows. The strategy selects step sizes based on the instantaneous energy dissipation rate and enforces monotonicity of a computable symmetric energy through a step rejection mechanism. We show that the step-size rules used in practice correspond to equidistributing a monitor function along the energy curve, connecting energy-adaptive time stepping to the classical theory of r-adaptive mesh methods. The monitor $g = |\dot{E}|$ is asymptotically optimal as it minimises the leading-order maximum symmetric-energy discrepancy for a given number of steps. A combined monitor that switches to $g = \sqrt{|\dot{E}|}$ near equilibrium caps step growth without degrading this error bound. The arclength parameter $β$ used in prior work is shown to be the ratio of the largest permitted step to the energy-error tolerance. The controller is paired with the SSAV--BDF2 discretization. Accepted steps satisfy monotonicity of the symmetric energy, from which we deduce a bound on the physical energy that is uniform in the number of steps, $\sup_n E(u^n) \le E(u^{0}) + τ_1 + O(Δt_{\max}^2)$, and the scheme achieves second-order global accuracy under standard step-ratio restrictions. Numerical experiments on Cahn--Hilliard, Ohta--Kawasaki, Phase--Field Crystal, and functionalized Cahn--Hilliard models confirm the theory and demonstrate the method's efficiency.

papers.title: Polynomial pathwidth for graphs vertex-coverable by few shortest paths and algorithms for quasi-shortest path covers
papers.abstract: We study how covering a graph by a small number of shortest or approximately shortest paths/walks constrains its treewidth and pathwidth. A path or walk is $(α,β)$-quasi-shortest for $α\geq1$ and $β\geq 0$ if each contiguous segment has length at most $α$ times the distance between its endpoints plus $β$. For graphs vertex-covered by $k$ shortest paths, we establish the first known polynomial pathwidth bound of $O(k^3)$. For edge-coverage, we improve the previously known $O(k^4)$ upper bound to $O(k^2\log k)$. As a main ingredient of the proofs, we first show that if the vertices of a graph can be covered by $k$ $(α,β)$-quasi-shortest paths or walks, then its treewidth is $O_{α,β}(k^2)$; this is a consequence of the fact that such graphs have linear metric growth and the technique developed in [Campbell et al., E-JC 2023]. To obtain the above pathwidth upper bounds, we combine this result with techniques from the literature in a nontrivial way. On the other hand, we show that there exist connected bipartite cubic graph whose edges can be covered by $k$ shortest paths and whose pathwidth is $Ω(k\log k)$, providing the first superlinear lower bound. For graphs covered by $k=2$ $(α,0)$-quasi-shortest paths with $α>1$, we show that, unlike treewidth and unlike the case $α=1$ and $β=0$ of exact shortest paths, the pathwidth may be unbounded. Finally, for every fixed rationals $α\geq1$ and $β\geq 0$, we give XP algorithms with a running time of $n^{f(k,α,β)}$ for some function~$f$ that decide whether the vertices of a graph can be covered by at most $k$ $(α,β)$-quasi-shortest paths or walks. The algorithms combine our treewidth upper bounds with an algorithmic meta-theorem from [Dreier et al., LICS 2025]. [abstract shortened to meet the arXiv requirements]

papers.title: Fefferman--Chang-type atomic decompositions for product Hardy spaces associated with Schrödinger operators
papers.abstract: We establish a geometric (Fefferman--Chang-type) atomic characterization of the two-parameter Hardy space associated with a pair of Schrödinger operators $L_i=-Δ+V_i$ on $\mathbb R^{n_i}$, $i=1,2$. The space is defined by the product conical square function. We assume comparability of neighbouring covering cubes, a local bound on the potentials, and decay of the semigroup mass at large scales. We prove that the Hardy norm is equivalent to a sum of classical local product Hardy norms at scales determined by the adapted coverings. This localization formula yields an atomic decomposition whose atoms satisfy size and partial cancellation conditions, with cancellation required only below the corresponding local scales. Both the atoms and their rectangular components remain supported inside fixed enlargements of the covering rectangles. The proof combines one-parameter Schrödinger Hardy space characterizations with standard vector-valued arguments and a localized product atomic decomposition with uniform control of scales and supports. The assumptions cover the model case of reverse Hölder potentials $V\in RH_q$, $q>n/2$, as well as potentials outside every $RH_q$ class, $q>1$, including half-space indicators and exponential potentials.

papers.title: Local Optimality of the d-cube for Laplacian Eigenvalues
papers.abstract: For each $d \ge 2$ we prove that the unit $d$-cube $\square_d \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ is, on the class $\mathcal{P}$ of convex polytopes combinatorially equivalent to a $d$-cube, (i) a strict local minimizer of the scale-invariant isoperimetric ratio $I(Ω) = \tfrac{P(Ω)^d}{|Ω|^{d-1}}$, with $P$ the perimeter, (ii) a strict local minimizer of the volume-normalized first Dirichlet eigenvalue $\barλ(Ω) = |Ω|^{2/d}λ_1(Ω)$, and (iii) a strict local maximizer of the volume-normalized first Neumann eigenvalue $\barμ(Ω) = |Ω|^{2/d}μ_1(Ω)$. The method is a shape-derivative Hessian analysis adapted to the hyperoctahedral symmetry of the cube. In symmetry-adapted coordinates on the parameter space --- the decomposition into irreducible representations of the hyperoctahedral group --- each Hessian is block-diagonal, with four scalar eigenvalues, which we give in closed form in $π$, rational coefficients, and a few universal series-constants. The first Neumann eigenvalue is not differentiable at $\square_d$, since its lowest cluster splits under perturbation. The Neumann case therefore works with a smooth auxiliary functional, whose Hessian is computed by second-order perturbation theory of the cluster; the coupling to modes outside the cluster enters at the same order. Finally, we show that extremality of $I$, $\barλ$, and $\barμ$ does not hold in high dimensions for a particular multilinear perturbation that leaves $\mathcal{P}$ by breaking convexity. All results are local; we discuss why a global statement, available for quadrilaterals (Endo and Osting, 2026), appears out of reach for $d \ge 3$.

papers.title: A smooth Riemannian metric on an arbitrary product of spheres with Bernoulli geodesic flow
papers.abstract: We construct a smooth Riemannian metric on an arbitrary product of spheres whose geodesic flow is Bernoulli with respect to the Liouville measure.
papers.comments: 81 pages, 8 figures. The main text and Appendices A and B occupy pages 1-46. Appendix C on pages 47-80 collects elementary but lengthy proofs of several claims and is intended to serve as a reference. Comments welcome!

papers.title: Classification of compatible left-symmetric conformal algebras on solvable Lie conformal algebras of rank two
papers.abstract: In this paper, we give a complete classification of compatible left-symmetric conformal algebra structures on solvable Lie conformal algebras which are free of rank two as $\mathbb{C}[\partial]$-modules up to isomorphism. We obtain ten mutually non-isomorphic normal-form types and determine the precise equivalence relations among the parameters within each family. Moreover, we also characterize the Novikov conformal algebras among the classified left-symmetric conformal algebras, thereby obtaining a complete classification of compatible Novikov conformal algebra structures in the same setting.

papers.title: An explicit elementary proof of no Landau--Siegel zeros
papers.abstract: We give an elementary proof of the absence of Landau--Siegel zeros with the explicit constant $c=1/100$. For every primitive quadratic Dirichlet character $χ$ of conductor $q\ge3$, each real zero $β\in(0,1)$ of $L(s,χ)$ satisfies $(1-β)\log q>c$. The proof combines integer coefficient counting, polynomial congruences, a paired-tail hyperbola estimate, and a logarithmically weighted comparison of positive sums. All required constants are explicit, and one choice of parameters covers every conductor. The argument uses elementary arithmetic and real summation and integration, without separate zero computations for small conductors.

papers.title: $\SL_3$ dual pairs
papers.abstract: We study the exceptional theta correspondence for dual pairs of the form $\SL_3\times G$ inside $p$-adic groups of type $E_n$, $n=6,7,8$. We establish Howe duality for lifts of all Whittaker-generic unitarizable representations of $\SL_3$. Our dual pair is in a see-saw relationship with a dual pair of the form $G_2 \times H$ such that $G/H$ is a rank-two symmetric space. Using the theta correspondence for $\SL_3 \times G$, we prove a multiplicity-one result for $H$-invariant functionals on representations of $G$.

papers.title: Finiteness theorems for Cayley permutation classes
papers.abstract: We prove that every hereditary Cayley permutation class with finitely many simple members has a finite basis and an algebraic generating function. We first show that every simple Cayley permutation of length at least two contains a simple pattern obtained by deleting one or two letters, and that the only exceptional Cayley permutations are the simple parallel alternations and their symmetries. We then characterize substitution-closed classes by the simplicity of their basis elements and show that classes with finitely many simple members are partially well ordered. Given the simple members and the basis of such a class, we construct a finite system of functional equations and compute an annihilating polynomial.

papers.title: Comb Tensor Network Finite-Difference Time-Domain Algorithms for 2D and 3D Electromagnetic Simulations
papers.abstract: This paper presents efficient 2D and 3D finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) algorithms augmented by the comb tensor network (CTN) representation of the field and auxiliary quantities. The proposed CTN-FDTD algorithm leverages superior compressibility of CTN compared with quantized tensor train (QTT), and rank-reduction strategies including local and global smoothing techniques to achieve logarithmic memory requirement and computation (per time step) cost. Numerical examples validate these complexities and demonstrate the applicability of CTN-FDTD using a variety of source excitation, frequency and permittivity profiles in both 2D and 3D. Remarkably, CTN-FDTD can simulate 35 trillion spatial grid points in 3D with low memory and computation costs on one computation node, whereas standard FDTD would require 281 TB memory to store each of its 31 3D arrays. Moreover, CTN-FDTD was applied to realistic 2D photonic crystal structure simulation with one million grid points and 3D scattering analysis with 8.6 billion grid points.

papers.title: A note on the proof of Barnette's conjecture
papers.abstract: Barnette's conjecture states that every cubic 3-connected bipartite planar graph has a Hamiltonian cycle. We present a digested exposition of OpenAI's generated proof of Barnette's conjecture \cite{openai-barnette}.

papers.title: Discovery of Singularities in Partial Differential Equations Using Adaptive Numerical Discretizations
papers.abstract: We compute self-similar singularity profiles of partial differential equations (PDEs) using adaptive numerical discretizations based on optimizing a discrete loss (ODIL). The fields are represented in overlapping local Chebyshev patches joined with a mapped asymptotic patch. After factoring out the leading power laws of solution ansatzes, their limiting amplitudes at infinity are determined by the optimization, eliminating domain truncation and prescribed far-field conditions. Adaptive refinement is guided by Chebyshev-coefficient decay, and the nonlinear least-squares problem is solved using automatically differentiated Gauss--Newton iterations with Levenberg--Marquardt damping. The method achieves O(10^{-14})-level accuracy for Burgers profiles, residuals of O(10^{-14}) to O(10^{-10}) for the generalized De Gregorio family, and of O(10^{-8}) in a local region for the two-dimensional Boussinesq equations. These results demonstrate that ODIL can identify singularity profiles for PDEs with high accuracy using adaptive numerical methods, complementing ongoing efforts that rely on artificial intelligence.

papers.title: Entropy bounded compact stencil Runge-Kutta discontinuous Galerkin method for hyperbolic conservation laws
papers.abstract: In this paper we introduce a compact stencil Runge-Kutta discontinuous Galerkin method for the Euler equations of compressible gas dynamics, which preserves a minimum entropy principle similar to that introduced by Tadmor for entropy solution of the Euler equations [4]. Compact stencil RKDG, introduced by Chen et al. in [15], is a variant of standard RKDG method which is known for its smaller stencil size and parallel efficiency. The main challenge is that the cRKDG method has to be expressed in Butcher form and not every Runge-Kutta method of this form is a convex combination of forward-Euler steps. Therefore, in order to establish this property we leverage the bound preserving framework of the cRKDG schemes [8], an entropy bounded limiter [6] and the classical positivity preserving limiter. In the last section numerical experiments are provided to demonstrate the robustness of the method.
papers.comments: Two dimensional results will be reported in revised version of the article

papers.title: An F-Type Normal-Reference Calibration for High-Dimensional Covariance Testing
papers.abstract: An F-type normal-reference calibration is developed for testing equality of two high-dimensional covariance matrices with unknown means. The test statistic is a ratio whose numerator measures the Frobenius covariance discrepancy and whose denominator estimates its null expectation. Their difference is the complete Li-Chen statistic. Under suitable moment and trace conditions, we establish a Gaussian-reference approximation. After standardization, the statistic and its reference share the normal or nonnormal limits determined by a convergent normalized spectrum. The reference is a ratio of independent chi-square-type mixtures. Applying Welch-Satterthwaite matching to its two components gives an ordinary F approximation, with degrees of freedom estimated from independent four-observation blocks. The effect of estimating the population means is controlled by an exact expansion, and local-power and consistency results are established. The ordinary F approximation is asymptotically valid under a diffuse spectrum, whereas a covariance spike can produce a nonvanishing approximation error. Simulation studies examine empirical size and power under normal and nonnormal sampling. Averaging the trace estimates over fixed partitions improves their stability, but does not remove size inflation in the strongly correlated settings.
papers.comments: 50 pages, 2 figures. Includes appendices and ancillary code

papers.title: When Language Models Misinterpret Uncertainty in Earth System Mechanism Attribution
papers.abstract: Mechanistic attribution in Earth system science requires quantifying uncertainty and communicating its implications. Here, we develop an uncertainty-aware mechanistic attribution pipeline that constructs probabilistic fingerprints from ensemble estimates, including covariance-aware separation of competing mechanisms, and an evidence ladder that systematically varies the information provided to language models (LLMs). We evaluate this framework in an idealized stochastic system and a coupled El Niño model using controlled interventions and ensemble data assimilation. In the idealized system, numerical separation increases GPT-4o's intervention-label agreement from 0.80 to 0.98, but not GPT-4o-mini's. In the coupled system, both LLMs identify seven of eight fingerprint-ambiguous events when given full fingerprints with verbal interpretations; GPT-4o's false ambiguity reports decrease from 10/82 to 1/82, without consistent gains in intervention-label agreement. For eight historical ENSO events, the uncertainty-aware condition agrees with the model-inferred mechanism labels in seven cases. These findings distinguish uncertainty assessment from its communication.

papers.title: The linearity Conjecture
papers.abstract: The Linearity Conjecture states that in the projective plane PG(2,$q$), $q=p^h$, every minimal blocking set (w.r.t. lines) is a linear point set over some subfield of ${\mathbb F}_q$. This paper contains the proof of the Linearity Conjecture for $p^e\ne 3,4$, where $e$ is the exponent of the blocking set. The text contains 3 concatenated parts. In Part 0, we give a guide for reading Parts 1 and 2. Part 1 develops a great part of the method, and the case $p^e=2$ is solved. In Part 2 we prove the Linearity Conjecture for $p^e\geq 5$.

papers.title: Drinfeld presentation of affine iquantum groups via iHopf algebras
papers.abstract: Affine quantum groups $\widetilde{\mathbf{U}}$ and affine iquantum groups $\widetilde{\mathbf {U}}^\imath$ admit two complementary descriptions: a Serre-type presentation and a Drinfeld (current) presentation. While iquantum groups $\widetilde{\mathbf {U}}^\imath$ are typically defined via the Serre presentation, their Drinfeld presentations are substantially more subtle and less well understood. In this paper, we give a conceptual derivation of the Drinfeld presentation of $\widetilde{\mathbf {U}}^\imath$ starting directly from the Drinfeld presentation of $\widetilde{\mathbf {U}}$, working within the framework of iHopf algebras. This approach leads naturally to the definition of iquantum affinization associated with arbitrary Kac-Moody algebras $\mathfrak{g}$. We further show that, in this general setting, these iquantum affinizations can be realized as coideal subalgebras of quantum affinizations with respect to the Drinfeld coproduct. Finally, in the affine case, we describe the imaginary root vectors $Θ_{i,r}$ of $\widetilde{\mathbf {U}}^\imath$ explicitly in terms of the root vectors $ψ^\pm_{i,r}$ of $\widetilde{\mathbf {U}}$, thereby extending the results of Li and Przeździecki for certain affine types of $\widetilde{\mathbf {U}}^\imath$.

papers.title: A Study in Solution Models for SAT using the PBNF-transform
papers.abstract: In this article, we use the PBNF-transform, or Polynomial Boolean Normal Form, described earlier in two articles and now extended to higher arity, to solve Boolean satisfiability problems (SAT), which are part of the P versus NP problem. SAT consists of a statement of conjunctions of clauses, and in our SAT-solving models, we dualize the logical equations, inverting the problem by \emph{multiplying} letters (literals) in the transferred clauses, now phrases: $pqrs\cdots s_{\ell}$, and using a binary iterated composition based on \emph{adding polynomials} for the conjunctions in our solution formula. We obtain Polynomial Boolean Equations, PBE=0, by also renaming the truth value $1\mapsto 0$(T). To find a solution, we look for repeating literals in the clauses to factor out. With reversed literal repetition, we can even reduce the CNF to the sum of the transformed clauses.

papers.title: LLM2Cert: LLM Synthesis of Certificates with SMT/Lean Verification
papers.abstract: Lyapunov functions and barrier certificates give state-space guarantees of stability and safety, but synthesizing and verifying them---especially for nonlinear, high-dimensional systems---remains an open challenge. Existing pipelines verify candidates with numerical solvers (sum-of-squares programs), interval methods, or satisfiability-modulo-theories (SMT) solvers, which often require relaxations, are conservative, or scale poorly with model dimension and nonlinearity. These limitations have also shaped benchmark design: standard test suites are dominated by low-dimensional polynomial systems chosen to suit what solvers can handle rather than what engineering applications require. We address both sides of this challenge. First, we introduce DynaCertBench, a benchmark of 105 instances: 80 non-redundant systems curated from the literature, extended with high-dimensional and control-constrained variants and new nonlinearly coupled systems, comprehensively spanning stability, region-of-attraction, forward-invariance, and safety tasks. Second, we present LLM2Cert, an LLM-driven framework that synthesizes candidate certificates and verifies them against their proof obligations: each obligation is routed to an SMT solver or directly to the Lean Proof-Repair agent. On DynaCertBench, LLM2Cert verifies 81 of 105 instances ($77.1\%$), a $17.1$ percentage point improvement over one-shot proposal without feedback. On the 81 fixed certificates, LLM2Cert verifies 22 that All-SMT leaves unresolved. Code and data are available at https://github.com/FormalCert-AI/llm2cert.
papers.comments: 59 pages, 3 figures. Equal contribution: Zhipeng Cao and Peiyang Song. Equal advising: Bai Xue and Alessandro Abate

papers.title: Supercritical magnetic ray transforms in hyperbolic space: the complexification method from the transport-twistor lens
papers.abstract: We present new inversion formulas for the unattenuated and attenuated magnetic ray transforms in the Poincaré disk, in the case of a constant, supercritical magnetic field. Our approach mirrors earlier complexification approaches by Novikov (Ark. Mat., 2002) and Bal (J. Math. Pures Appl., 2005), and a second feature of this article is to connect the approach with the Transport Twistor framework recently introduced by Bohr-Paternain (J. Éc. polytech. Math., 2023; arXiv:2606.25173).

papers.title: The reverse Ritz inclusion: computable bounds on the pseudospectra of an operator by those of a finite-rank compression
papers.abstract: We consider a bounded operator on a separable complex Hilbert space, reached only through its action on vectors and that of its adjoint, and split it along a subspace of finite dimension into a compression, a far block acting on the complement, and the two couplings between them. Given upper bounds on the norms of the couplings and of the far block, we show that outside a disc a pseudospectrum of the operator lies in a pseudospectrum of the compression, with an explicit loss in the level; this reverses the classical inclusion of the Ritz values in a pseudospectrum of the operator. The same bounds, with the smallest singular value of the shifted compression, bound the resolvent of the operator, count its eigenvalues with algebraic multiplicity inside every contour outside the disc on which a computed inequality holds, and enclose its spectral projector; no normality, self-adjointness or positivity is used.
papers.comments: 34 pages, 4 figures. Data: doi:10.7910/DVN/HOZFS8. Code: https://github.com/JuliaBallArithmetic/RigorousPseudospectra.jl (tags reverse-ritz-arxiv-v1, reverse-ritz-arxiv-v2) and https://github.com/JuliaBallArithmetic/BallArithmetic.jl (tag reverse-ritz-arxiv-v1)

papers.title: High-Order Fully Discrete Entropy-Stable DG Methods with Compact Explicit Single-Step Time Discretizations
papers.abstract: We develop a unified framework for high-order, fully discrete entropy-stable discontinuous Galerkin (DG) methods with compact explicit single-step time discretizations. At the end of each time step, the preliminary DG polynomial is scaled toward its cell average to enforce a strong cell entropy inequality while preserving conservation. This correction is feasible if and only if the updated cell average satisfies a weak cell entropy inequality, which standard third-order strong-stability-preserving Runge--Kutta DG updates can violate at arbitrarily small positive CFL numbers. For compact single-step schemes, including compact Runge--Kutta, Lax--Wendroff, and ADER-DG methods, we derive an explicit interval of feasible numerical entropy fluxes at each interface and prove that it is nonempty under a CFL condition. Projecting a compatible high-order target flux onto this interval guarantees the weak cell entropy inequality and preserves single-step high-order accuracy on smooth solutions, including near nondegenerate extrema. The limiter also enforces multiple entropy inequalities simultaneously. We also establish a Lax--Wendroff-type theorem. Numerical experiments for scalar conservation laws and the compressible Euler equations demonstrate high-order accuracy, multi-entropy control, and robustness for strong shocks.

papers.title: Matrix Triangle Inequalities: Past, Present, and Future
papers.abstract: This survey provides a concise overview of matrix triangle inequalities. Classical topics, such as inequalities for unitarily invariant norms, are revisited from a different perspective, with a particular emphasis on unitary orbit inequalities and various notions of matrix moduli. The exposition progresses from elementary results to much more recent developments, highlighting the evolution of the subject and its ongoing directions of research.
papers.comments: accepted in Reviews in Mathematical Physics

papers.title: Dynamics of the Liquidity Profile in Concentrated Liquidity Provision: An SPIDE Approach
papers.abstract: We model the dynamics of the liquidity profile in Uniswap~V3 and other concentrated-liquidity automated market makers with a stochastic partial integro-differential equation (SPIDE). The profile, the aggregate of all provider positions across tick space, evolves under a degenerate Sturm--Liouville operator, which encodes mean-reverting concentration around the market price, coupled with a Hilbert--Schmidt integral operator, which captures nonlocal redistribution driven by provider repositioning. We establish existence and uniqueness of the mild solution in a weighted $L^2$ space built on the Gegenbauer eigensystem, and reduce the SPIDE to a coupled system of linear stochastic differential equations whose low-order modes describe the level, slope, and curvature of the profile. Pairing the SPIDE with a log-price process yields tractable expressions for pool reserves, pool value, and loss-versus-rebalancing under Ornstein--Uhlenbeck-type and Black--Scholes-type noise. A finite-rank calibration in a fixed reference frame, applied to three Uniswap pools, gives interpretable estimates and lowers active-band forecast error relative to a martingale benchmark on the two pools compatible with the stationary specification. On the third pool, out-of-sample diagnostics are consistent with nonstationarity, which motivates price-aware and time-varying extensions.

papers.title: Rigid and $τ$-locally free modules via Taft algebras
papers.abstract: We show that rigid modules are $τ$-locally free for a large family of 1-Iwanaga--Gorenstein algebras. This family includes many cases of the algebras introduced by Geiss--Leclerc--Schröer in their Inventiones paper "Quivers with relations for symmetrizable Cartan matrices I: Foundations", hence answering a question posed by Geiss--Leclerc--Schröer for many new cases. Our result is achieved by introducing coactions of Taft algebras and applying the recent theory developed by the first-named author and Coulembier.

papers.title: Very tight embeddings of subspaces of \(L_p\) for \(0<p<1\)
papers.abstract: For \(0<p<1\) and \(μ>1\), every \(d\)-dimensional subspace of \(L_p\) embeds linearly into \(\ell_p^{\lfloorμd\rfloor}\) with distortion at most \(C(p,μ)(\log(d+2))^{1/p}\). If its Rademacher type \(q\) constant is at most \(T\), where \(p<q\leq2\), the distortion is at most \(C(p,q,μ)T\), independently of \(d\). We also give explicit bounds as \(μ\downarrow1\). This answers the question of Johnson and Schechtman concerning the extension of their very tight embedding theorem below exponent one. The proof combines compression at a lower exponent with a change of density that preserves the number of coordinates, and applies over both scalar fields.

papers.title: Localizing Restriction Categories
papers.abstract: The localizing/separating factorization, which is the analogue, for restriction categories, to the surjective/embedding factorization for topoi, is developed at both the mere restriction category and join restriction category level. The factorization system at both the ordinary and join level is approached using the notion of a density, which is a stable and universal suborder of the restriction order. The main technical results of the paper construct the join localization and establish its basic properties. The paper gives several examples of localizations. In particular, examples of localization on commutative rigs are provided which give a way to construct categories of schemes. The Zariski spectrum and the Pierce spectrum are, in particular, developed.

papers.title: Return Time Sets of Minimal Points for Countable Group Actions
papers.abstract: For a countably infinite discrete group $G$, we study subsets of $G$ that contain a neighbourhood return-time set of a minimal point in a $G$-flow $X$. For $e\in F\subseteq G$, we characterize this property by the existence of $e\in A\subseteq F$ such that $\operatorname{Int}_K(A):=\{t\in G:Kt\subseteq A\}$ is right syndetic for every finite $K\subseteq A$, and equivalently by the support of a minimal binary configuration in the Bernoulli shift $2^G$. Additional conditions on $\operatorname{Int}_K(A) \operatorname{Int}_K(A)^{-1}$ characterize realization by minimal flows that are weakly mixing of all finite orders or strongly mixing: for every such $K$, the former requires that for each finite $H\subseteq G$ there is $c\in G$ with $HcH\subseteq \operatorname{Int}_K(A) \operatorname{Int}_K(A) ^{-1}$, whereas the latter requires that $\operatorname{Int}_K(A)\operatorname{Int}_K(A)^{-1}$ be cofinite. We also construct, for every compact metrizable minimal $G$-flow, a free minimal, strongly mixing Cantor flow disjoint from it.

papers.title: Computable presentations of separable Lebesgue spaces
papers.abstract: For every right-c.e.\ real $p\in(1,2)$, $L^p[0,1]$ has a computable presentation. The proof combines an effective stability modulus for almost isometric embeddings with a Fraïssé-style construction in which the exponent varies. In the same range, if $\ell^p$ has a computable presentation, then $p$ is computable. Combining these with the known results gives the computable presentability classification for all separable Lebesgue spaces. We also formulate an effective Fraïssé theorem for Banach spaces and apply it to obtain a computable presentation of the Gurarij Banach space.

papers.title: Collinear motions in constant curvature spaces, and coplanar motions in $\mathbb{R^4}$
papers.abstract: A collinear motion of an $n$-body problem is one in which the $n$-bodies always lie along some, possibly moving, geodesic during their evolution. We prove that every collinear motion of $n\geq 3$ bodies in a constant non-zero curvature space is necessarily contained in some fixed constant curvature space of dimension at most three. For natural systems admitting energy and angular momentum integrals, we further show that every such motion is necessarily a relative equilibrium: evolving under uniform rotation while maintaining constant mutual distances. These results extend certain classical results on collinear motions in Euclidean spaces, initiated by P. Pizzetti, to general spaces of constant curvature. The same methods also yield a partial answer to a question of A. Wintner. Namely, we show that any concave and always coplanar motion in the Euclidean 4-body problem, where the moving plane containing the bodies sweeps out an $\mathbb{R}^4$, must be self-similar: maintaining constant mutual distance ratios over the motion.

papers.title: Non-aware computable presentations of randomizations
papers.abstract: Let 2 be the two-element structure in the empty signature. We build a computable presentation Q of the Borel randomization $2^{[0,1)}$ in which neither constant random variable is a computable point. Consequently, Q is not aware. This gives a negative answer to a question of Cuervo Ovalle and Goldbring \cite{CG}. We also construct a countable structure $M$ with no computable presentation but $M^{[0,1)}$ has a computable presentation. This answers another question and establishes the necessity of the awareness condition stated in one of the main theorems in \cite{CG}.

papers.title: Asymptotics of local height pairing without Hodge conjecture
papers.abstract: We remove the assumption of the Hodge conjecture from the asymptotic formula for the Archimedean local height established in our previous work. We also remove other minor assumptions. We achieve this by exploiting the cohomological nature of Beilinson's local intersection index rather than arguing motivically.

papers.title: Scattering theory for bulk and surface waves in an impedance half-space, II: local perturbations, the scattering matrix and an inverse problem
papers.abstract: We study the Robin, or impedance, Laplacian on a half-space of dimension $n \ge 3$ which is perturbed inside a fixed ball. The boundary may be deformed, and obstacles may be present in the interior or attached to the boundary, in any combination and with no smallness assumption. Outside the ball the configuration is the flat impedance half-space of Part I, with constant impedance $α> 0$, where a bulk channel and a surface channel propagate at every positive energy and only the surface channel propagates on the band $(-α^2,0)$. We prove a limiting absorption principle, valid at every positive energy and outside a discrete set of embedded eigenvalues in the band. We construct the generalized Fourier transform and prove its completeness by a stationary argument which constructs no wave operator and reduces completeness to the uniqueness of the scattering solution at each energy. We then obtain the scattering matrix, its unitarity and a two-channel optical theorem. The main result is a uniqueness theorem for the inverse problem. Under two geometric conditions on the pair, the scattering amplitude at a single positive energy determines the perturbation completely, and the argument does not distinguish a deformation of the boundary from an obstacle. It follows that no nontrivial perturbation satisfying the same conditions is invisible at any positive energy. On the surface band the corresponding statement is reduced to one explicitly stated question about the exterior Robin problem.
papers.comments: 74 pages, 2 figures. Part II of a two-part series; Part I is arXiv:2610.27885

papers.title: Explicit Measurable Counterexamples to Finite-Difference Equations
papers.abstract: We study finite-difference operators of the form \[ D(f,h)=\sum_{k=1}^n a_k f(b_kh), \] where the coefficients may be complex and the nodes are real. Ash, Catoiu, and Csörnyei characterized the finite differences for which \[ D(f,h)=o(h)\quad\Longrightarrow\quad f(h)=o(h) \] holds for every measurable real-valued function. We extend their counterexample theorem to complex-valued functions defined on \(\mathbb C\). Except for the same exceptional four-term configuration, we construct a Lebesgue measurable function \(f\) such that \[ D(f,h)=0\qquad\text{for every }h\in\mathbb C, \] while \(f(h)\not=o(1)\) as \(h\to0\). The counterexamples are supported on countable multiplicative subgroups. The construction is based on zeros of Laurent polynomials and multiplicative characters, and avoids the infinite-dimensional linear-algebra argument used in the earlier proof.

papers.title: Soft-Update MSA for Nonconvex Stochastic Optimal Control: Theory and Algorithms
papers.abstract: For the method of successive approximations (MSA), a fundamental challenge is that the stochastic maximum principle (SMP) provides an optimality condition rather than a descent rule. To overcome this difficulty for nonconvex stochastic control problems, we develop a soft-update MSA (SU-MSA) with a second-order-adjoint correction of the Hamiltonian and a neural realization called DeepSMP. Both an explicit stepsize rule guaranteeing cost descent and the convergence of the algorithm are established. Moreover, the global SMP condition is asymptotically satisfied when the corrected Hamiltonian is convex, while in a special case the cost is further proved to converge to the global optimum. To extend SU-MSA to high dimensions, we develop DeepSMP using a differentiable smooth approximation of the corrected Hamiltonian and analyze the convergence of the resulting objective and its gradient. Numerical experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework.

papers.title: Explicit meromorphic solutions of certain types of nonlinear differential-difference equations
papers.abstract: Our main purpose is to determine all meromorphic solutions, in explicit form, of the nonlinear differential-difference equations \begin{equation*} f^{n}(z)f'(z)+q(z)f(z+c)=p_{1}{\rm e}^{α_{1}z}+p_{2}{\rm e}^{α_{2}z} \end{equation*} and \begin{equation*} f^{n}(z)f'(z)+q(z){\rm e}^{Q(z)}f(z+c)=p_{1}{\rm e}^{α_{1}z}+p_{2}{\rm e}^{α_{2}z}, \end{equation*} where $n\geq 3$ is an integer, $q(z)$ and $Q(z)$ are nonzero polynomials with $Q(z)$ nonconstant, and $c,~p_{j},~α_{j}(j=1,2)$ are nonzero constants satisfying $α_{1}\neq α_{2}$. We sharpen the result in the cited literature, as illustrated by specific examples.

papers.title: Weighted boundedness of maximal operator associated with invertible linear transformations on variable Lebesgue spaces
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the boundedness of $M_{A^{-1}}$, the maximal operator involves an invertible matrix, on the weighted variable spaces $L^{p(\cdot)}(w)$, where the weights are in an appropriate class. In general, we obtain the necessary conditions for the weight classes and exponents. However, for certain types of invertible matrices, we characterize the weights such that the boundedness holds.

papers.title: The dual complex and RC-invariant functors
papers.abstract: We extend the dual complex of a simple normal crossings divisor to a homotopy type invariant $\mathcal{D}(X)$ of arbitrary complex varieties, and we prove that it is contractible when $X$ is connected and of klt type. In fact, the dual complex belongs to a broader class of invariants, which we call RC (rationally connected)-invariant functors. We prove a rigidity theorem governing the behavior of such functors with respect to rationally connected fibrations.

papers.title: Asymptotically Sharp Length Thresholds for \texorpdfstring{$q$}{q}-ary Codes with Distances \texorpdfstring{$2$}{2} and \texorpdfstring{$4$}{4}
papers.abstract: For an integer $q\ge5$, let $A_q(n,\{2,4\})$ be the largest cardinality of a subset of a $q$-ary Hamming space of length $n$ in which every two distinct words have distance $2$ or $4$. Set \[ N(q)=\left\lceil\max\left\{2q+1, \frac{17+\sqrt{8q^2+96q-95}}2\right\}\right\rceil. \] We prove that $A_q(n,\{2,4\})=1+\binom n2$ for every $n\ge N(q)$. In particular, $N(q)=2q+1$ for $q\ge26$. An explicit code of size $q(n-2)$ shows that the least eventual threshold $N_*(q)$ satisfies $N_*(q)\ge2q-1$; consequently $2q-1\le N_*(q)\le2q+1$ for every $q\ge26$. The argument applies to arbitrary integer alphabet sizes, without a linearity assumption.
