papers.abstract: For a closed embedded minimal hypersurface in a unit sphere, we show that the existence of a uniform vanishing angle in Lawlor's criterion suffices for its cone to minimize area. The normal-wedge condition follows from Howard's rolling theorem. We derive explicit curvature bounds and apply them to the reported Hsiang-Sterling curvature estimates for topologically trivial cones. The resulting area-minimizing cones give an affirmative answer to the existence question raised by Ilmanen and White (Camb. J. Math., 2015).

papers.title: A sharp diameter-mass inequality on Einstein manifolds and ADM mass
papers.abstract: Let $(M^n,g), n\geq 4$ be a close Einstein manifold with positive scalar curvature and $G$ be the Green function of the conformal Laplacian. The ADM mass of the asymptotically flat metric $\hat g:=G^{4/(n-2)} g$ is an important geometric invariant. When either $n=5$ or $n\geq 6$ with Weyl vanishing condition, we prove a mass formula, generalizing Gursky-Malchiodi's formula in dimension $4$. An important step is an extension of Viaclovsky's Green function expansion in higher dimensions. Next we prove a sharp diameter-mass inequality on Einstein manifolds. Finally we present two applications. First, we prove a mass gap theorem for Einstein manifolds. Second, for Collins-Székelyhidi's family of Sasaki-Einstein metrics $g_i$ on $\mathbb{S}^5$ with volume going to zero, the sequence of the masses $m(\hat{g_i})$ blows up uniformly as $i\to\infty$.

papers.title: Endpoint weighted Fourier estimate with vanishing spherical trace
papers.abstract: We establish an endpoint weighted Fourier estimate under a vanishing restriction condition on the unit sphere. Let $n \geq 2$ and $p_c = 2(n+1)/(n+3)$. We prove that every $f \in L^{p_c}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ with zero spherical Fourier restriction satisfies $$ \left\| \bigl|1-|ξ|^2\bigr|^{-1/2}\widehat{f}(ξ) \right\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^n)} \leq C_n \|f\|_{L^{p_c}(\mathbb{R}^n)}, $$ where the restriction condition is understood through the continuous Tomas--Stein restriction operator. This result gives a negative answer to Goldberg's counterexample-existence question and supplies a missing endpoint.

papers.title: Sum-rank analogues of Reed--Muller codes over Abelian Galois extensions
papers.abstract: Let $\mathbb L/\mathbb K$ be a finite Abelian Galois extension with a fixed decomposition $\mathrm{Gal}(\mathbb L/\mathbb K)=\langleσ_1\rangle\times\cdots\times\langleσ_m\rangle$. We show that the quotient of the multivariate skew polynomial ring $\mathbb L[x_1,\ldots,x_m;σ_1,\ldots,σ_m]$ by suitable central polynomials $H_1(x_1),\ldots,H_m(x_m)$ is isomorphic to a product of $t$ copies of $\mathrm{End}_{\mathbb K}(\mathbb L)$, so that one skew polynomial represents all blocks of a sum-rank metric space. The sum-rank weight of an element equals the rank of an associated Dickson matrix and of a generalized Moore matrix. Using this, we define sum-rank Reed--Muller-type codes and show that their dimension and minimum distance are given by the formulas for affine Cartesian codes with side lengths $\mathrm{deg}\,H_1,\ldots,\mathrm{deg}\,H_m$; the same holds for codes supported on lower sets. The family contains as special cases linearized Reed--Solomon codes, Gabidulin codes, rank-metric Reed--Muller codes, and affine Cartesian codes. Over finite fields, every linearized Reed--Muller code of Berardini and Caruso is, after a monomial change of variables, a monomial code in our framework. This gives the dimension of all these codes, and their exact minimum distance in every degree whenever the support is a lower set.

papers.title: Gradient Discrete Schrodinger Bridge Matching for Peptide Generation
papers.abstract: The optimal control of a discrete Schrödinger bridge is a discrete gradient, a difference of vertex potentials, but recent models such as MadSBM instead learn a free control on the edges by cross-entropy. We prove that this leaves the action uncontrolled: cross-entropy identifies the control only up to a state-dependent shift (a gauge), and the action is $\operatorname{KL}(r\|p)$ plus a gauge term the loss never constrains. We propose GDSBM, which writes the control as a difference of vertex potentials and adds the action to the loss; pinning the gauge costs no expressiveness and makes the action a property of the model, so the penalty acts on the model and not on the gauge. On peptide generation our MadSBM reimplementation has a free-gauge action of order $10^{8}$ for a gauge-fixed value of $6.5$, against $1.5$ for GDSBM, with no quality loss that three seeds can detect. The gradient form also fits guidance, which becomes the addition of a potential: guided toward a net charge of $+3$ at pH~7, GDSBM is closer than MadSBM, over three seeds, to its exact tempered target in total variation at every guidance strength (at $β=1$, $81\%$ of samples in the target window against $74\%$, for a target of $97\%$); we claim no statistical significance.

papers.title: A new lower bound for the sixth Schur number: $S(6)\ge 537$
papers.abstract: We give an explicit partition of $\{1,\ldots,537\}$ into six sum-free sets, establishing $S(6)\ge 537$. This improves the lower bound 536 of Fredricksen and Sweet (2000). Known recursive constructions then give the improved lower bounds $S(8)\ge 5\,372$, $S(11)\ge 204\,208$, $S(13)\ge 2\,042\,082$, and $R_6(3)\ge 539$. We also report 131 pairwise inequivalent partitions found by the search. We describe their structure and provide the complete partitions in the supplementary material. These partitions provide starting points for future searches and structural studies of Schur partitions.

papers.title: A second-order linear decoupled scheme with a relaxed zero-energy variable for Rayleigh-Bénard convection
papers.abstract: We construct a second-order, linear, and fully decoupled scheme for Rayleigh--Bénard convection between Navier-slip walls. The nonlinear terms are treated explicitly and multiplied by a scalar with exact value $1$ and no energy contributed to the continuous problem. As a result, each BDF2 step, with a rotational pressure correction, solves only constant-coefficient linear problems. For the time discretization, we prove that, for any time-step, the energy decays when the walls have equal temperatures, under a condition on the thermal weight, and the energy is bounded on finite time intervals when heated from below. Relaxing the scalar towards $1$ preserves both estimates. Energy stability does not control the accuracy of the scalar; the velocity and temperature fields are computed with its unrelaxed value, whose deviation from $1$ scales like $(E/C)(δt/τ)^3$ for kinetic energy $E$, time-scale $τ$ of the flow, and weight $C$ of the scalar equation. In our tests, choosing $C$ comparable to $E$ keeps this deviation small and doubles the largest time-step for which steady rolls are reproduced to a relative difference of $10^{-8}$. With Taylor--Hood elements, we observe second-order convergence in time, recover the critical Rayleigh numbers, and match published Nusselt numbers to within $0.5\%$. A three-dimensional implementation passes corresponding validation tests.

papers.title: Integral representations of high-order derivatives of Bessel functions with respect to the order
papers.abstract: We derive integral representations for the $n$-th derivative with respect to the order of Bessel functions of the first, second and third kinds, as well as the modified Bessel function and the Macdonald function. Based on these integral representations, we have developed a highly-efficient algorithm for the numerical evaluation of these derivatives with respect to the order, applicable to any complex argument and any real order.

papers.title: Sharp stability for the Talenti inequality
papers.abstract: We prove a sharp quantitative version of the Talenti rearrangement inequality. Specifically, we show that, for any $p\in [1;+\infty]$, for any $f\in L^\infty(Ω),\, f\geq 0,\, f\not\equiv 0$, for any open set $Ω\subset \mathbb{R}^d$ with finite volume, the solution $u_{f,Ω}$ to $-Δu_{f,Ω}=f,\, u_{f,Ω} \in W^{1,2}_0(Ω)$, satisfies, in dimension $d\geq 1$, $\Vert u_{f^\sharp,Ω^\sharp}\Vert_{L^p(Ω^\sharp)}-\Vert u_{f,Ω}\Vert_{L^p(Ω)}\gtrsim α(Ω)^2+\inf_{z\in \mathbb{R}^d}\mathscr A(f,z)^2$ and, in dimension 1, $ \Vert u_{f^\sharp,Ω^\sharp}\Vert_{L^p(Ω^\sharp)}-\Vert u_{f,Ω}\Vert_{L^p(Ω)}\gtrsim α(Ω)+\inf_{z\in \mathbb{R}}\mathscr A(f,z)^2$ where $α(Ω)$ denotes the Fraenkel asymmetry of $Ω$, $\mathscr A(f,z)$ a weighted asymmetry of $f$ with respect to some center $z$ and $Ω^\sharp$ (resp. $f^\sharp$) is the Schwarz rearrangement of $Ω$ (resp. of $f$). In dimension $d\geq 2$, this estimate implies $ \Vert u_{f^\sharp,Ω^\sharp}\Vert_{L^p(Ω^\sharp)}-\Vert u_{f,Ω}\Vert_{L^p(Ω)}\gtrsim α(Ω)^2+\inf_{z\in \mathbb{R}^d}\Vert f-f^\sharp(\cdot-z)\Vert_{L^1}^2.$ Our result sharpens and extends recent quantitative versions, and does not rely on shape differentiation arguments, but on a generalisation of the quantitative Saint-Venant inequality.

papers.title: Adaptive Local Proper Orthogonal Decomposition via Graph Partitioning and Provable Error-Bounded Lossy Compression for Parametric Series in Finite-Dimensional Function Spaces
papers.abstract: We introduce a spatially adaptive proper orthogonal decomposition (POD) method for error-bounded lossy compression of snapshot data in finite-dimensional function spaces. The method combines hierarchical graph partitioning with independent low-rank approximations on spatial subdomains, allowing the local approximation ranks to adapt to the spatial distribution of information in the data. For partitions that are orthogonal in the discrete inner product, we establish an exact decomposition of the global squared reconstruction error into local contributions and characterize the optimality of the resulting local POD approximations for fixed partitions and ranks. These results provide a rigorous mechanism for allocating a prescribed global error tolerance among subdomains and selecting the smallest admissible local ranks. We further develop a sufficient error bound for the coefficient-space normalized root-mean-square error (NRMSE). A greedy hierarchical refinement algorithm accepts a spatial subdivision only when it reduces the storage required by the local low-rank factors while preserving the prescribed reconstruction-error bound. The method is assessed using synthetic data and snapshot sequences from two- and three-dimensional compressible-flow simulations. The numerical results illustrate how spatially adaptive ranks and partitioning can improve compression relative to global POD and fixed spatial partitions, particularly when the data exhibit spatially heterogeneous dynamics.

papers.title: The Penrose Correspondence over a Non-Archimedean Field
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be a non-Archimedean local field of characteristic different from $2$ and let $V$ be a four-dimensional symplectic $K$-vector space. We study the Penrose incidence correspondence $\mathbb{P}(V) \leftarrow \mathrm{Flag}(1,2;V) \rightarrow \mathrm{Gr}(2,V)$ after Berkovich analytification. The Klein quadric $\mathrm{Gr}(2,V)$ decomposes into the open orbit $\mathrm{Spin}(5)/\mathrm{Spin}(4)$ and the Lagrangian quadric, which parametrize respectively the projective lines transverse and tangent to the standard contact distribution on $\mathbb{P}(V)$. We construct explicit free discrete subgroups $Γ\subset\mathrm{PSp}(V)$ and analytic domains, cut out by Drinfeld upper half-spaces, in all three members of the incidence diagram. Both incidence projections are surjective on these domains, the three $Γ$-actions are free and properly discontinuous, and the Penrose double correspondence descends to the analytic quotients. The quotient of the twistor domain is a contact analytic threefold, and the Grassmannian domain is contained in the analytification of the $\mathrm{Spin}(5)/\mathrm{Spin}(4)$ open orbit.

papers.title: Bounded symbols and one-component geometry
papers.abstract: We prove that every bounded truncated Toeplitz operator on a Hardy model space admits a bounded symbol if and only if its defining inner function is one-component, meaning that it has a connected sublevel set at some level in $(0,1)$. This resolves the bounded symbol conjecture of Baranov, Chalendar, Fricain, Mashreghi and Timotin and, through known equivalences, the embedding and weak factorization conjecture of Baranov, Bessonov and Kapustin. A uniform bound $R$ for the ratio of least bounded symbol norm to operator norm on the rank-one family associated with point evaluation in the disk already forces this geometry. The corresponding bound for all bounded truncated Toeplitz operators is at most $CR\log(e+R)$, where $C$ is absolute, and the logarithmic factor is optimal. In a nonzero de Branges space, the same geometric condition characterizes when every sufficiently small equivalent change of norm preserving the de Branges structure is represented exactly by reweighting the original integral with a positive density bounded above and away from zero. This characterization remains valid when the norm changes are restricted to discrete sampling norms. Outside the one-component class, every model space admits self-adjoint trace class truncated Toeplitz operators without bounded symbols, with arbitrarily small norm and singular values satisfying any prescribed positive upper bounds.
papers.comments: 29 pages. All results first posted 7 Oct 2026, https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23214254

papers.title: Convex Equilibrium Potentials for Monge--Ampère: Curvature Bounds and A Posteriori Evaluation
papers.abstract: Equilibrium neural networks define their hidden state as the fixed point of a contraction, so their effective depth is set at evaluation time rather than by the architecture. Using them for fully nonlinear PDEs raises two issues that explicit networks avoid: second derivatives may grow with the effective depth, and the potential is only ever evaluated approximately. We study nonnegative softplus equilibrium networks with contraction factor $q<1$, a convex class suited to the Monge--Ampère equation. A positivity cancellation in the resolvent shows that the Hessian grows at most like $(1-q)^{-2}$, rather than the $(1-q)^{-3}$ of a direct estimate, and an explicit one-neuron family shows that this exponent is sharp; third derivatives satisfy a sharp $(1-q)^{-3}$ bound. Residual-based a posteriori estimates then control the state, its input derivatives and, in two dimensions, the Hessian determinant at an approximate equilibrium. Combined with interval arithmetic on complete covers of the domain, they yield rigorous uniform bounds on the Monge--Ampère residual and, through a comparison argument, on the solution error of a fixed trained network. On two manufactured Dirichlet problems on the unit disk, all six trained models are certified with residual below $0.25$ and boundary error below $0.01$. Adaptive stopping halves float64 evaluation time at best, whereas certified adaptive evaluation remains costlier than fixed depth.

papers.title: Lower bounds on Steklov eigenfunctions for a class of curvilinear polygons
papers.abstract: Steklov eigenfunctions, $\{φ_{σ_j}\}_{j=0}^\infty$, are the eigenfunctions of the Dirichlet to Neumann map on a bounded domain with eigenvalue $σ_j$. This paper considers Steklov eigenfunctions and eigenvalues on a family of curvilinear polygons, $Ω_α$ whose boundaries are smooth away from a single corner of angle $α$. We (i) prove optimal lower bounds on the decay of the harmonic extension, $u_{σ_j}$, of $φ_{σ_j}$ away from the boundary of $Ω_α$ and (ii) give optimal lower bounds on the degree to which the high energy Steklov spectrum of $Ω_α\setminus H_1$ may differ from that of $Ω_α\setminus H_0$ when $H_1$ and $H_0$ are isometric. This shows that the corresponding estimates in recent work by the authors together with Malagutti are optimal. The proof in this paper was obtained through an interaction with ChatGPT 6 Astra: While writing the work with Malagutti, the authors became curious about optimal error bounds for the difference between the Steklov spectra on a curvilinear polygon, $P$, and the spectrum of any operator which knows only local information about $\partial P$. The authors suggested to ChatGPT to remove two isometric, smooth domains from a curvilinear polygon. ChatGPT suggested the ideas for a proof based on a regularized trace and the singularity in the kernel of the DtN map near a corner. The authors then suggested a simpler, conformal approach, the method for handling small angles, and the idea to obtain lower bounds on Steklov eigenfunctions. The paper is entirely written by the authors and the argument has been significantly modified, clarified, and simplified from the ChatGPT ideas.

papers.title: Stability of Fourier Restriction for a Class of Finite Type Surfaces in $\mathbb R^3$
papers.abstract: We establish the stability of the optimal non-endpoint Fourier restriction range under smooth flat perturbations of curved-root surfaces in $\mathbb R^3$. Specifically, we consider graphs of $$φ(x_1,x_2)=(x_2-x_1^m)^n+R(x_1,x_2),$$ where $m,n\ge2$ are integers and $R$ is smooth and flat at the origin. On a sufficiently small neighborhood depending on the perturbation, we prove the local $L^p(\mathbb R^3)\to L^2(S,dσ)$ restriction estimate for $1\le p<p_c$, where $$p_c=\frac{q_c}{q_c-1}, \qquad q_c=\max\left\{2+\frac{2mn}{m+1},2n\right\}.$$ If the nonnegative localizing density is positive at the origin, an adapted-box example shows that the estimate fails for $p>p_c$. Thus arbitrary smooth flat perturbations preserve the optimal restriction range away from the critical endpoint. For $n\ge3$, the main local estimate combines planar curve decoupling with a one-dimensional finite-type extension estimate, whose principal scale factors cancel exactly. For $n=2$, we prove a uniform $C^4$ perturbation estimate using a weighted convolution bound and an anisotropic Whitney decomposition. Anisotropic rescaling and summation complete the proof.

papers.title: Bridging persistence of discrete and continuous 1D maps: Total variation, permutation equivalence, and diagonal affine transformations
papers.abstract: Fundamental to the field of topological signal processing (TSP) is the \textit{persistence diagram} (PD), or barcode, of a signal, which gives noise-resistant measures of topologically significant features as distinct from noise. Existing literature proves that the total persistence computed from these diagrams is equal to the total variation, for certain continuous signals on compact domains. We provide a closed formula for this shared quantity, and generalize to all continuous and discrete functions on bounded domains, and to certain functions on non-compact 1D manifolds. Extending the identification of continuous and discrete persistence, we investigate the similarities of functions with the same PDs, and prove that, for any $n$, the persistence diagram can be calculated as a function of the sequence of critical values; we compute these formulas for $n \leq 6$. Finally, we examine which function transformations cause predictable changes in the PD of the transformed function, characterizing affine and linear transformations.

papers.title: Local-Cohen-Macaulay DG-rings with unequal finitistic projective dimensions
papers.abstract: For every pair of integers $d,n\geq1$, we construct a commutative noetherian local-Cohen-Macaulay DG-ring $A$ such that $\dim H^0(A)=d$, $\mathrm{amp}(A)=n$, $\mathrm{fpd}(A)=d-n$, and $\mathrm{FPD}(A)=d$. This gives a negative answer to the implication from local-Cohen-Macaulayness to equality of the two finitistic projective dimensions in a question of Bird, Shaul, Sridhar, and Williamson.

papers.title: Control, stability, and stabilization of some classes of linear time-delay systems
papers.abstract: This monograph presents a selection of the author's recent works on the control, stability, and stabilization of some classes of linear time-delay systems. After a detailed introduction to topics related to time-delay systems covered in the monograph, its main contents are presented in a series of mostly independent chapters.

papers.title: An asymptotic $Γ$-BMT inequality
papers.abstract: We refine a bound of Cheng-Feyzbakhsh to prove an asymptotic $Γ$-Bayer-Macrì-Toda ($Γ$-BMT) inequality on every smooth polarized complex threefold. The proof relies on a reduction to small tilt stability parameters. Using this inequality we verify Feyzbakhsh-Thomas's condition $(wBG)$ whenever $K_{X}$ is numerically proportional to the polarization. For polarized Calabi-Yau threefolds, this yields a reduction of positive rank generalized Donaldson-Thomas (DT) invariants to those counting sheaves pure in codimension one. We further express these invariants in terms of rank one generalized DT invariants. Thus, the rank reductions of Feyzbakhsh-Thomas hold without assuming the BMT conjecture.

papers.title: Landau-Siegel zeros over a base field and effective Brauer-Siegel
papers.abstract: Let k be a number field. We prove that for every quadratic extension F/k, every real zero beta of L(s, chi_{F/k}) satisfies (1 - beta) log d_F >= c(k) with an effective constant c(k) > 0, and we deduce (through a reduction of Stark) that the Brauer-Siegel theorem holds effectively and uniformly over all Galois extensions K of k, in the form h_K R_K >= c(k) d_K^{1/2} / ((2 pi)^{[K:Q]} log d_K). Stark's effective cases of the Brauer-Siegel theorem were the fields without quadratic subfields, since the quadratic subfields carried the ineffectivity of Siegel's theorem; over a base field k, the first result removes it. Both rely on a uniform bound for Chebotarev sums. Let K/k be a Galois extension with group G, and suppose S is a subset of G containing the identity. For any prime p of k, let delta_p be the proportion of the primes of K above p whose Frobenius lies in S. Then the sum over Np <= X of delta_p log Np / Np is at most (|S|/|G| + epsilon) log X + O(1), uniformly in K, as soon as X >= d_K^C with C depending only on epsilon and the degree [K:Q]. The proof is Kerr's form of the OpenAI argument, simple vanishing at the points (iota theta)_{iota in S}, with theta in a box in O_K, and Masser's zero estimate. The field enters only through Masser's invariant of the lattice of points, which we compute to be [K:Q]/|S| by averaging over the Galois group of the normal closure. Over Q, the determinant method of Green, Barreto, and Kominers gives sharper Chebotarev bounds, and we explain the comparison.

papers.title: Benign cubic and quartic forms on the sphere
papers.abstract: One considers the NP-hard problem of minimizing real cubic and quartic forms on the Euclidean unit sphere. One first extends the Hessian spectral characterization of local minima by the author. In particular one provides a gap-depth characterization of negative global and spurious minima, and proves that the minimum value of an odd degree-d form is recovered (up to the factor d(d -1)) by minimizing the smallest eigenvalue of its ambient Hessian over the sphere (and equivalently the unit ball). Next, one exhibits several classes of benign families of cubic and quartic forms (i.e. with no spurious local minima on the sphere) and prove that some are robust to small coefficient perturbation (i.e. the resulting form remains benign even if it leaves the initial family). Therefore the class of benign cubic and quartic forms is full-dimensional (in the ambient space of coefficients), for n $\ge$ 2. Also for every odd degree d, the class of benign degree-d forms increases with the dimension (however it does not imply that such forms become more frequent when the dimension increases).

papers.title: Concavity of the Ornstein--Uhlenbeck torsion function on centered ellipses and its failure on convex domains
papers.abstract: Let $u$ be the torsion function of a bounded domain $Ω$ in $\mathbb{R}^n$ for the Ornstein--Uhlenbeck operator, that is, the solution of $-Δu + x\cdot\nabla u = 1$ in $Ω$ with $u=0$ on the boundary. We prove that for every $n\ge2$ there are bounded, centrally symmetric domains whose torsion function is not concave. These domains have boundary with a flat piece and can be smoothed so that the boundary is $C^\infty$, strictly convex with principal curvatures bounded below by a positive constant, while keeping the torsion function not concave. In contrast, the torsion function for every ellipse centered at the origin is concave, and for every ball centered at the origin we prove the sharp bound $D^2u\leq-\frac{1}{n}I$. The ellipse result follows by deformation from the disk, using a boundary flux estimate and third-order boundary identities to exclude a first zero eigenvalue of the Hessian.

papers.title: The symmetric skew monoidal structure of Gray-categories
papers.abstract: In a previous paper, we constructed a closed skew monoidal structure on the category of Gray-categories and Gray-functors whose internal hom Psd(A, B) captures pseudomaps and pseudo-transformations. In the present paper we give a symmetric description of the Gray-category Psd(A,B) and use this to prove that the skew monoidal structure is symmetric skew monoidal.

papers.title: The center is the formal internal automorphism group
papers.abstract: We prove that the deformation functor associated to an algebra over a sufficiently nice Koszul operad can be lifted to an operadic formal moduli problem over the Koszul dual operad. We further show that this operadic formal moduli problem corresponds to the derived center of the algebra under the operadic Lurie-Pridham correspondence. As an application, we prove that the classical Gerstenhaber algebra structure on polyvector fields of a commutative algebra agrees with the derived center of the algebra as an abelian Poisson algebra.
papers.comments: 19 pages. Revised and expanded version of Section 5.4 of the author's Ph.D. thesis, arXiv:2607.05455. Comments welcome

papers.title: A Resource Allocation Tournament
papers.abstract: We introduce and analyze a round-robin simultaneous resource allocation contest, motivated by sports leagues and other competitive environments where agents must distribute limited resources across multiple encounters. Players allocate resources in advance to matches against all opponents, and match outcomes are determined by relative allocations. We study two payoff schemes: total points, where players accumulate rewards for each win, and winner-takes-all, where only the tournament winner is rewarded. For three players, we provide complete equilibrium characterizations under both schemes. For four or more players, we show that the total points payoff admits Blotto-type equilibria, while the winner-takes-all payoff requires numerical and algorithmic analysis. To address this, we develop a best-response dynamics algorithm with stochastic inertia and use it to approximate equilibria in games with four and five players.

papers.title: A hybrid finite-volume scheme with learned rational reconstructions and exact nonlocal fluxes for the space-fractional Burgers equation
papers.abstract: On coarse grids, fronts of fractional conservation laws can be narrower than one cell, while the flux through each face depends on the whole domain. For the forced space-fractional Burgers equation, we write the finite-volume defect exactly, with the Riesz flux acting as a nonlocal interface flux. Our proposed closure, NRC, is decoder-only, since the encoder is the exact cell-average projection and a small network only maps cell averages to a sub-cell reconstruction. The decoder adds rational atoms with learned complex poles to a trigonometric histopolant, preserves every cell average, and has closed-form advective and Riesz fluxes. We prove that the scheme conserves mass for every value of the weights and that the learned sub-grid flux has a dipole tail. On 64 cells, NRC reaches a median test error of 0.0308% over three seeds, against 0.431% for WENO5-Z and 0.153% for a black-box flux correction. Ablations show that the exact global operator, the projection and the sub-grid Riesz flux carry most of this gain, and most sub-cell fronts carry a deep learned pole within a quarter cell. NRC keeps its advantage over WENO5-Z under shifts of the order and the forcing and, when trained on several diffusivities, under the tested diffusivity shifts by factors from 0.6 to 2.5 in the median over seeds. From 32 to 128 cells, NRC stays an order of magnitude more accurate than WENO5-Z on the same grid. This gain lies in accuracy per degree of freedom and in an interpretable closure.

papers.title: Dimension-free regimes for unadjusted Langevin in ridge-separable models: A subspace robust Wasserstein analysis
papers.abstract: The Unadjusted Langevin Algorithm (ULA) is widely used for high-dimensional Bayesian inference. Classical analyses in Wasserstein-2 distance predict an asymptotic bias and a mixing time that grow with dimension, but this metric is stronger than necessary for many statistical tasks. We instead analyze the bias in subspace robust Wasserstein distance, which controls the mean and arbitrary low-dimensional marginals and is therefore well suited to observables typically estimated in practice. For ridge-separable potentials formed with i.i.d. data, we prove high-probability bounds showing a bell-shaped mixing profile as the number of data points $N$ varies relative to the dimension $d$. In the overparameterized regime, the effective dimension is the rank $N$ of the data-dependent perturbation, leading to complexity depending on $N$ rather than $d$. In the large-sample regime, Gaussian-perturbation estimates yield dimension-free complexity once $N$ is sufficiently large. In contrast, near the proportional regime $\asymp d$, we prove that dimension-free guarantees are impossible in general.

papers.title: A special Hardy estimate in the axisymmetric swirl problem
papers.abstract: We examine the proof of Dongyi Wei's logarithmic circulation criterion. A trace estimate specific to $\nabla(u_r/r)$ replaces a generic squared-swirl form bound by one with one logarithm rather than two. Repeating the coupled $J$--$Ω$ energy and comparison argument then gives a proposed threshold of order $(\log D)^{-5/4}$. Under the hypotheses stated below, the proof is intended to establish regularity when $|r u_θ|\le C|\log r|^{-α}$ uniformly near the axis with $α>5/4$, and at $α=5/4$ with an absolute sufficiently small coefficient. Every analytic step, including the cutoff core and exterior terms, is included for independent checking.
papers.comments: With the help of an OpenAI Dot, we quickly obtained preliminary results. We subsequently found that a manuscript by Stan Palasek (arXiv:2610.29012) presents essentially the same main results. However, the technical approaches differ, particularly in the squared-swirl estimate, which is substantially shorter in our manuscript. We will further refine and polish the manuscript

papers.title: Random Survivor Sets with Moving Holes in Bedford-McMullen Carpets
papers.abstract: Let $2\le m < n$ be integers, and let $K(\mathcal{A})$ be the Bedford--McMullen carpet generated by $\{(x,y)\mapsto((x+i)/m,(y+j)/n):(i,j)\in\mathcal{A}\}$, where $\mathcal{A}$ is a subset of $\{0,1,\ldots,m-1\}\times\{0,1,\ldots,n-1\}$. Write $\mathcal{B}$ for the set of occupied columns, and assume that $\#\mathcal{B}\ge2$ and each column contains at least two symbols of $\mathcal{A}$. At each vertex of the column tree $\mathcal{B}^*$, we independently choose one forbidden symbol from $\mathcal{A}$ according to a prescribed distribution. Let $\mathbb{P}$ denote the resulting product measure on $\mathcal{A}^{\mathcal{B}^*}$. This gives a random survivor set $K_ω(\mathcal{A})$ with $ω\in\mathcal{A}^{\mathcal{B}^*}$. We show that, for $\mathbb{P}$-a.e. $ω$, \begin{equation*} \dim_H K_ω(\mathcal{A})=\frac{1}{\log m}\log\left(\int \sum_{b\in\mathcal{B}}\ell_b(ω)^{\frac{\log m}{\log n}} d\mathbb{P}(ω)\right), \end{equation*} where $\ell_b(ω)$ is the number of surviving symbols in column $b$ at the root.

papers.title: Local heights for nef toric compactified divisors
papers.abstract: We present a definition of a local height of nef toric divisors in the sense of Yuan and Zhang by approximating a height for canonical divisors and then using the local energy to extend to other metrics on the same geometric divisor.

papers.title: Boundary regularity of $k$-Hessian eigenfunctions
papers.abstract: We prove smoothness up to the boundary for $k$-Hessian eigenfunctions on smooth bounded uniformly convex domains when $2\leq k<n$. This resolves an open problem in the regularity theory of degenerate fully nonlinear elliptic equations and extends the boundary smoothness theorem for Monge--Ampère eigenfunctions. In contrast to the Monge--Ampère case, the linearized $k$-Hessian operator remains uniformly elliptic up to the boundary.

papers.title: Semi-strict 4-categories as enriched categories
papers.abstract: We introduce several flavours of semi-strict 4-category as enriched categories. We give the axioms for semi-strict 4-categories in elementary terms and describe a wide range of examples. In particular, we answer the question of what exactly Gray-categories and the higher transformations between them form: namely, a left-sharp 4-category G-Cat$^4$. In addition, we describe examples arising from braided monoidal 2-categories, monoidal Gray-categories (herein defined) and Gray-categories with structure. We use the concepts introduced here and the relationships between them to unify various concepts in the literature, such as Crans' 4-teisi. In the second part of the paper, we investigate homotopical aspects. In particular, we classify the equivalence n-cells in the left-sharp 4-category G-Cat$^4$ for each n. Using this, we show that the left-sharp skew monoidal structure on the category of Gray-categories induces a symmetric monoidal closed structure on the homotopy category of Gray-categories.

papers.title: Concentration inequalities for vector-valued martingales
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish several deviation inequalities for the norms of vector-valued martingales, achieving bounds of the same quality as those available in the classical one-dimensional setting. Our results extend and refine previous work by Pinelis (1994) and Hayes (2005) in this area.

papers.title: A Fast Algorithm for Quaternion Tensor Singular Value Decomposition under the T-product
papers.abstract: Quaternion tensor singular value decomposition (T-SVD) under the T-product provides a framework for analyzing multidimensional quaternion data. However, the T-SVD construction of Pan and Ng (SIAM J. Matrix Anal. Appl., 2024) \cite{PanNg2024} contains a structural gap: an unrestricted quaternion matrix SVD need not preserve the paired Fourier block structure required for tensor factor recovery, potentially leading to loss of T-unitarity and inaccurate reconstruction. To address this issue, we develop a structure-preserving construction that transforms each paired quaternion block into a complex matrix and maps its complex SVD factors back to quaternion factors with the required structure. This construction corrects the proof of \cite[Theorem 4]{PanNg2024} and leads to a corrected version of \cite[Algorithm 2]{PanNg2024}, hereafter referred to as the ``corrected algorithm'', ensuring T-unitary tensor factors and an f-diagonal core for arbitrary third-order quaternion tensors. A numerical counterexample demonstrates the failure of \cite[Algorithm 2]{PanNg2024} and verifies the corrected algorithm at machine precision. Notably, we propose a fast structure-preserving algorithm, Algorithm~\ref{alg:t-fast}, and compare it numerically with the corrected algorithm. The experimental results show that Algorithm~\ref{alg:t-fast} reduces the decomposition time while maintaining near-machine-precision accuracy. Furthermore, its application to color video encryption yields high reconstruction quality, favorable ciphertext statistics, and stability under input perturbations.

papers.title: Concavity-Free $L^\infty$ Estimates and Stability for Fully Nonlinear Complex Equations
papers.abstract: In this paper, we extend the $L^\infty$ estimates of Guo-Phong for fully non-linear equations on compact hermitian manifolds to a possibly indefinite reference form satisfying a uniform admissibility criterion. Furthermore, we also establish one-sided stability estimates. Neither result requires homogeneity or concavity of the nonlinear operator.

papers.title: On exact solutions to three-dimensional Yukawa lattice model and BCC to FCC phase transitions
papers.abstract: We determine the global minimizers of the three-dimensional Yukawa lattice energy at every fixed density. At unit covolume, BCC is the unique minimizer below a transition parameter $κ_*\approx1.7179218684699$, FCC is the unique minimizer above it, and exactly these two lattice classes minimize at the transition. Mathematically, denote the Yukawa potential and the energy per particle under this potential by \[ v_κ(r)=\frac{e^{-κr}}r,\qquad E_κ(L)=\frac12\sum_{v\in L\setminus\{0\}} \frac{e^{-κ|v|}}{|v|}. \] Then, \[ \arg\min_{|L|=1}E_κ(L)= \begin{cases} \hbox{BCC lattice},&0<κ<κ_*, \hbox{BCC or FCC lattice},&κ=κ_*, \hbox{FCC lattice},&κ>κ_*. \end{cases} \] As a consequence, the zero-screening comparison recovers the unique BCC minimum for the renormalized Coulomb energy.

papers.title: Deep holes of full-length Reed--Solomon codes: uniform bounds and exact classifications
papers.abstract: Let $u$ be a received word for the full-length Reed--Solomon code $\operatorname{RS}_q(k)$, with interpolation polynomial $f_u$ of degree $k+m$. For each $m\in\{3,4,5,6,7\}$, we classify all such deep holes over every finite field, without a field-size hypothesis. None occur for odd $m$ in this range. At $m=4$ and $m=6$, the only exceptions are, respectively, the Segre sextic and Frobenius-power families; these occur only in dimension two over fields of characteristic two. For arbitrary $m\geqslant3$, we also establish two uniform bounds. If $\sqrt q\geqslant12(m+1)\log(2m+2)$, no word of interpolation degree $k+m$ is a deep hole when $q$ is odd, $k\geqslant3$, or $m$ is odd. If $q>16(m+2)^4$, we obtain the corresponding complete classification at every admissible $k$, including the explicit dimension-two exceptions. Our proofs use an agreement criterion expressed in complete homogeneous symmetric functions, agreement-count estimates, finite geometry, permutation-polynomial restrictions, and subset constructions for solving the resulting symmetric-function equations. The remaining finite cases are settled by finite computations with supplied certificates and deterministic verification programs.

papers.title: Uniform coarse ellipticity, $A_2$ weights, and boundary regularity
papers.abstract: We study symmetric divergence form elliptic equations with measurable coefficients that may be degenerate and unbounded, under a uniform bound on the coarse ellipticity ratio over all ambient cubes and scales. We prove that uniform coarse ellipticity and classical $A_2$ weighted ellipticity define incomparable coefficient classes. For every admissible choice of coarse parameters, we construct a scalar weight with a logarithmically corrected, locally integrable singularity along a product Cantor set. Its codimension is chosen according to the upper coarse discount exponent, and the resulting coefficient satisfies the uniform coarse condition but is comparable to no $A_2$ weight. Conversely, an explicit $A_2$ weight fails the coarse condition for every admissible parameter choice. Under uniform coarse ellipticity we give a direct PDE treatment of boundary regularity in the approximable energy realization. Using coarse interior estimates, we prove boundary decay and solvability of the continuous Dirichlet problem in bounded NTA domains. An almost-positivity argument, with energy approximation and boundary testing justified, yields boundary Harnack and Hölder continuity of quotients of positive solutions with common zero boundary values. The argument requires no additional energy Sobolev inequality and avoids the construction of Green functions. Further examples distinguish uniform coarse control from finite coefficient moments and from coercivity on $\mathrm L^2(\mathrm{d} x)$. We also record interior Hölder estimates and continuity criteria under nonuniform control along nested scales.

papers.title: Pólya's conjecture for Neumann eigenvalues of spherical shells
papers.abstract: We prove the strict Pólya inequality for Neumann eigenvalues of spherical shells in every dimension $d\ge2$, for every radius ratio and every positive energy. The proof also covers balls. For shells, the excess over the leading Weyl term has a positive lower bound depending only on dimension. Above explicit frequency thresholds independent of the radius ratio, we obtain a surplus of boundary order. These estimates remain uniform as the hole shrinks or the shell becomes thin. We compare weighted sampling errors for inverse radial actions while retaining the removed volume exactly. The proof is entirely analytic and requires no computer-assisted verification.

papers.title: A sphere obstruction for the Hilbert shift quotient
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal H=\ell^2(\mathbb Z)$ and let $\mathbb Z$ act by bilateral shifts. We prove that the quotient $\mathbb S(\mathcal H)/\mathbb Z$ of the unit sphere, equipped with its quotient metric, has infinite Hilbert distortion. Consequently, $\mathcal H/\mathbb Z$ does not admit a bilipschitz embedding into Hilbert space, answering a question of Cahill, Iverson, and Mixon. The proof first embeds every flat torus $\mathbb R^n/L$, after rescaling, into the quotient $\mathbb S\big(\ell^2(\mathbb Z^n)\big)/\mathbb Z^n$ with distortion arbitrarily close to $1$, where $\mathbb Z^n$ acts by translations. We then show that every finite subset of this quotient embeds into $\mathbb S(\mathcal H)/\mathbb Z$ with distortion arbitrarily close to $1$. The lower bounds of Khot and Naor for the Hilbert distortion of flat tori then imply the result.
papers.comments: The proof of the main theorem was found using OpenAI's ChatGPT 5.5

papers.title: Prime Nullspace Matrices and Even Dominating Sets
papers.abstract: A non-zero $m \times n$ (0, 1)-matrix $A$ is called a {\em nullspace matrix} if each entry $(i, j)$ of $A$ has an even number of $1's$ in the set of entries consisting of $(i, j)$ and its rectilinear neighbors. These matrices correspond to even dominating sets of $m \times n$ grid graphs. We study these matrices and consider those that cannot be constructed from smaller nullspace matrices.

papers.title: Asymptotic observable symmetry for spacetime observability of waves I: The disc
papers.abstract: Building on the spacetime observable symmetry discovered in NWX (2025), we introduce asymptotic observable symmetry (AOS) for the wave equation. Its central object is a family of generated approximate velocities constructed from fixed profiles, carrying the same propagation-induced symmetry at different scales and asymptotically realized by exact waves. We investigate AOS on the disc through radial propagation and reflection. This gives a family of spacetime measurable observation sets satisfying the essential spacetime measurable geometric control condition for a fixed positive observation time. However, the observability inequality fails on each of these fixed sets.

papers.title: Homogenization of the Stokes equations with slender bodies
papers.abstract: In this paper we study the convergence of solutions of the Stokes equations in a domain perforated by slender bodies placed on a fixed periodic grid of size $2ε$ as the size of the bodies goes to zero and the number of bodies goes to infinity. We assume that the width $b_ε$ of the bodies vanishes faster than the length $a_ε$ of the particles. We identify the critical scaling regimes for $a_ε$ and $b_ε$ and prove that in this case the system is effectively described by the Brinkman equations.

papers.title: From Quaternions to Pentarnions I: Algebra, geometry, and a spin model
papers.abstract: We introduce a family of five-dimensional non-flexible quadratic real algebras $\{\mathcal A_γ\}_{0\leqγ\leq1}$ with canonical basis $1,i,j,k,\ell$, in which $γ$ changes the multiplication but not their norm, and study how this change affects geometry and dynamics. The algebras are pairwise non-isomorphic, $\mathcal A_0$ contains Hamilton's quaternion algebra, and $\mathcal A_1$ is the Pentarnion algebra. The alternating part of the trilinear form $\langle u\times_γv,w\rangle$ induced by the multiplication of $\mathcal{A}_γ$ defines a three-dimensional subspace $H_γ\subset\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb R}\{i,j,k,\ell\}$, tilted by the angle $\arctan(γ/\sqrt3)$, whose rotation group $G_γ\cong\mathrm{SO}(3)$ contains the automorphism group of $\mathcal A_γ$. For $γ_1\neγ_2$ the groups $G_{γ_1}$ and $G_{γ_2}$ generate $\mathrm{SO}(V)\cong\mathrm{SO}(4)$. For the six ways of ordering and bracketing the product of $i,p,p$ in $\mathcal A_γ$, two map the unit circle in ${\rm span}\{j,k\}$ to a point and, for $γ>0$, four map it to ellipses. As an application, we derive a Hamiltonian model of a classical spin on $H_γ$ whose multiplication-induced quadratic energy is isotropic for $γ=0$ and anisotropic for $γ>0$. It conserves spin length and, for fixed $γ$, energy, and satisfies an exact work identity when $γ$ varies in time. Numerical experiments with periodically varying $γ$ indicate both regular and irregular spin dynamics.

papers.title: Effective Dual Subgradient Methods Through Sequential Subgradient-Aligned Rays
papers.abstract: In this paper, we propose an efficient subgradient-based framework, referred to as the sequential subgradient-aligned rays (SSAR) method, for improving the convergence performance of the dual subgradient method. In particular, the proposed method identifies and exploits a finite sequence of rays, when available, as the dual subgradient method evolves, along each of which a subgradient of the negative dual function remains constant and aligns with the ray. While the dual variable iterates remain on each identified ray, a constant stepsize associated with the ray is employed, with the associated constant stepsizes decreasing from one ray to the next. This approach yields constant decrements in the negative dual function values while the dual variable iterates remain on the associated rays, enabling the dual variable iterates to progress more quickly toward a dual optimal solution. We then show that the proposed SSAR method can be leveraged to improve the performance of the dual decomposition method for minimizing the average of local loss functions associated with multiple agents that share a common decision variable, a widely used problem formulation in many large-scale real-world applications. In particular, the SSAR method improves the convergence performance of the corresponding dual decomposition method while also reducing its communication cost. Numerical experiments on a least squares regression problem and a logistic regression problem using real datasets are conducted to evaluate the performance of the SSAR method.
papers.comments: This work has been submitted to the IEEE for possible publication

papers.title: Conservative Finite Element Methods for Kirchhoff-Type Equations
papers.abstract: We construct and analyse a fully discrete scheme for a Kirchhoff-type nonlinear integro-differential equation in two spatial dimensions with time-dependent coefficients. The scheme combines a symmetric three-layer time discretization of Crank--Nicolson type with a conforming finite element method of arbitrary polynomial degree $p$ and a Picard iteration for the nonlinearity. We prove that the Picard iteration is well defined and, that the iterates converge to the Ritz projection of the exact solution measured in fractional-power norms of the discrete Laplacian. Running the same energy argument in the unshifted norms, and under the same hypotheses, we then obtain the optimal order $\mathcal{O} ( h^{p+1} + τ^2 )$ in $L^2$ and $\mathcal{O} ( h^{p} + τ^2 )$ in $H^1$ for the full error. For the homogeneous problem with constant coefficients, the exact solution of the scheme moreover preserves a discrete energy identically. Numerical experiments with manufactured solutions reproduce the predicted second order in time and the full spatial order $h^{p+1}$ in the $L^2$-norm.

papers.title: Improved Bounds for the Entropic Central Limit Theorem in the Log-Concave Case
papers.abstract: Let $μ$ be a log-concave isotropic probability measure on $R^d$ , and let $μ^n$ denote the law of the normalized sum of $n$ independent random vectors with law $μ$. We prove that \[ H(μ^n|γ)\leq \frac{C}{n} \min\left\{1+\log(ed)^2H(μ|γ)\ ,\ d\right\}. \] Compared to the previous best known bound, our estimate replaces the polynomial dependence on the dimension by a polylogarithmic one. The proof relies on a new combination of the De Bruijn identity with Eldan's stochastic localization process.

papers.title: Mixed-Precision Coalesced Matrix-Free Multigrid with Vertex-Patch Smoothing
papers.abstract: I present a geometric multigrid solver for the Poisson equation with continuous cubic elements in three dimensions, smoothed by a multiplicative vertex-patch Schwarz method with exact local solves. All fields are kept in persistent cell-wise storage, where every cell holds its own copy of each shared degree of freedom. The patch smoother yields a continuous solution without any exchange between cells. On the GPU, the patch update is computed in registers, one cell per thread, and the cells of a patch exchange data by warp shuffles, so shared memory is avoided almost entirely. Despite the low occupancy that this design implies, the arithmetic of the patch update runs close to the FP32 peak. Fast diagonalization, merged transforms, and a reflection symmetry of the patch then reduce the arithmetic until a sweep moves its data at $87\%$ of the bandwidth of a plain device copy. The hierarchy therefore runs in single precision inside a double-precision outer iteration. Rounding the unassembled residual destroys the cancellation between opposite-sign copies of shared degrees of freedom; exchanging the copies between cells in double precision performs this cancellation before rounding, without changing the dual vector they represent. With this \emph{rebalancing}, the cycle converges as in double precision and independently of the mesh size, the error converges at the optimal rate down to the precision of the solve, and the solver reaches over $400$ million degrees of freedom per second on a single NVIDIA A100 GPU.

papers.title: A semiampleness result for hyperkähler fourfolds and smoothings of Lagrangian subvarieties
papers.abstract: We give a geometric proof of the following statement: let $X$ be a smooth hyperkähler fourfold such that the Picard group is generated by a line bundle $L$ that is nef, non-trivial, and not big. If the Kodaira dimension of $L$ is non-negative, some positive multiple defines a Lagrangian fibration. The proof requires a number of tools which are of independent interest, including an analogue of Voisin's unobstructedness result and a smoothing result for singular Lagrangian subvarieties.

papers.title: Water Transport on 3-Spiders: Unbounded Lengths of Shortest Optimal Strategies
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a finite simple graph. An averaging operation selects a nonempty connected vertex set and replaces the weights of its vertices by their arithmetic mean. For a nonnegative initial weight function $ω:V(G)\to\mathbb R_{\ge0}$ and a target vertex $x$, let $t(G,x,ω)$ denote the minimum number of averaging operations needed to attain the maximum reachable weight at $x$. Gollin et al.[1] proved, using the Axiom of Choice, that a finite optimal strategy exists for every finite graph, every nonnegative initial weight function and every target vertex; see Tao [2] for a simplified proof. We prove that the lengths of shortest optimal strategies on $3$-spiders have no uniform finite bound. In particular, these lengths cannot be bounded in terms of the maximum degree of the graph.

papers.title: Douglas-Rachford splitting method for nonconvex stochastic optimal control
papers.abstract: Motivated by the numerical resolution of stochastic optimal control problems, particularly those involving nonlinear dynamics, we investigate the convergence properties of the Douglas-Rachford splitting algorithm in a nonconvex and infinite-dimensional setting. We introduce an extension of the method that applies when one component of the objective function is continuously differentiable with a locally Lipschitz gradient, while the other is weakly lower semicontinuous with a bounded domain.

papers.title: Maximum Likelihood Estimation and Likelihood Ratio Tests for the Power Spherical Distribution
papers.abstract: The Power Spherical distribution has been proposed as a computationally efficient alternative to the von Mises-Fisher distribution for data on the unit sphere, with reduced computational cost for simulation and a simpler normalizing constant. Despite these advantages, its statistical inference properties remain underdeveloped. In this paper, we develop a likelihood-based framework for estimation and inference for the Power Spherical distribution. Within this framework, we develop maximum likelihood estimation procedures for both the central direction and concentration parameter. Building on these estimators, we formulate likelihood ratio tests for hypotheses involving known and unknown parameters, study their asymptotic behavior, and evaluate finite-sample performance through simulation studies. The results demonstrate accurate Type I error control and good power when the asymptotic chi-square approximation is appropriate, while the parametric bootstrap provides reliable inference in small-sample settings or those where the dimension is large relative to the sample size. The findings also highlight nontrivial dependence of the power of tests for the central direction on the concentration parameter.

papers.title: Structure-preserving reduced-order models of thin panels in supersonic and hypersonic flow
papers.abstract: We build structure-preserving reduced-order models for both challenge problems of the AePW-4 High-Speed Working Group. They are a clamped thin panel at Mach 1.92 (RC-19) and a cantilever plate at Mach 5.85 (HyMAX). The published data for each case hold no time-resolved response and no repeated runs. The physics must therefore be carried by the form of the model. One construction gives two models per problem. A Ritz-Galerkin reference model describes the plate. A learned model keeps the reference model's exact potential, fits the remaining generalized forces, and trains only a dissipation that cannot add energy. Its energy balance holds for any weights by construction. On the trained model the worst relative residual is 2.2e-15. On RC-19, shock relations predict a pressure ratio of 1.521 across the panel. Pressure-sensitive paint measured the same value. Thirty runs of the learned model place the mean dominant frequency within 1.0% of the measured 236 Hz. At one periodic and one chaotic condition, the learned model reproduces the response regime of a published reduced-order model in all sixteen runs. It does so without that model's 113 Hz spectral peak, which the measurements do not show. Measured displacements can also correct the chaotic response through one more force that respects the energy balance. We tested this on synthetic data at the experiment's 5 kHz sampling rate. The state error is 1.25% of the panel thickness without noise and 3.5% with 10 micrometers of noise. On HyMAX the learned model follows the reference model's trailing-edge displacement for 65 ms with a relative error of 3.7%. These results show that a model whose structure carries the physics can match measured flutter behavior when the available data cannot train it.

papers.title: Closing All-Exp Gaps in Local Search for the Traveling Salesman Problem and Maximum Constraint Assignment
papers.abstract: We prove the all-exp property for the Traveling Salesman Problem with the $2$-opt neighborhood, and for $(3,2,2)$- and $(2,3,2)$-Maximum Constraint Assignment with the flip neighborhood. The all-exp property states that infinitely many instances have an initial solution from which every sequence of improving moves to a local optimum, and hence every run of local search, has exponential length. For the Traveling Salesman Problem, the all-exp property was previously known for every $k$-opt neighborhood with $k \ge 3$, so our result for $2$-opt completes the picture for all $k$-kopt neighborhoods. In $(p,q,r)$-Maximum Constraint Assignment, each constraint involves at most $p$ variables, each variable occurs in at most $q$ constraints, and each domain has size $r$. Decreasing any of the parameters of $(3,2,2)$ or $(2,3,2)$ yields a problem in which every sequence of improving flips has polynomial length, so both Maximum Constraint Assignment results are tight. All three results settle long-standing open problems. Our proofs build on a common construction idea, which reveals a close connection between the local-search dynamics of the three problems.

papers.title: Functions determining $(q+3)/2$ directions over the finite field with $q$ elements
papers.abstract: Let $q=p^n$, where $p>2$ is prime. We prove that every $q$-set $U\subseteq\mathrm{AG}(2,q)$ determining exactly $(q+3)/2$ directions is affinely equivalent to the graph of $x^{(q+1)/2}$. For $n\ge2$, we also prove that a $q$-set determining at most $(q+p)/2$ directions is either an affine $\mathbb{F}_p$-linear set or affinely equivalent to this graph. The classification for $n=1$ is due to Lovász and Schrijver. For $n=2$, the classification and the stated stability result follow from results of Gács, Lovász, and Sz\H onyi and the direction theorems of Blokhuis, Ball, Brouwer, Storme, and Sz\H onyi, completed by Ball. These direction theorems establish affine $\mathbb{F}_p$-linearity for functions with fewer than $(q+3)/2$ determined directions. Our proof uses Rédei polynomials, results of Gács, Lovász, and Sz\H onyi on their coefficients, and an earlier polynomial comparison lemma of the author.

papers.title: Liouville-type theorems and perturbation uniqueness for stationary incompressible MHD with directional fractional dissipation
papers.abstract: We study Liouville-type theorems for stationary solutions of the incompressible magnetohydrodynamics equations in $\mathbb{R}^n$, with directional fractional dissipation $(-\partial_i^2)^αu$ and $(-\partial_j^2)^βb$, where $n\ge 2$ and $0<α,β\le 1$. We prove that $u\equiv b\equiv 0$ by assuming that $u\in L^{p,\infty}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ and $b\in L^{q,\infty}(\mathbb{R}^n)$, with suitable conditions on $p$ and $q$. The proof uses a localized fractional energy identity and does not assume finiteness of the global homogeneous Sobolev energy. The method also applies to the case of full fractional dissipation. For the system with common-directional fractional dissipation, we prove stationary uniqueness for compactly supported perturbations of arbitrary smooth transverse shear backgrounds when $0<α,β<1$. We also establish a quantitative uniqueness criterion for perturbations of backgrounds with bounded gradients that are not necessarily compactly supported, for all $0<α,β\le 1$, assuming directional localization.

papers.title: Direct Inference on Admissible Sets (Diona)
papers.abstract: We propose a new regression method named Direct Inference on Admissible Sets (Diona) that directly uses samples to estimate the state and its derivatives at a query point, along with their admissible bounds, without long global training. By casting the values and derivatives at the query and neighbouring samples as latent variables in a constrained optimisation problem, the burden of long training loops becomes one of on-demand local solves. We establish Diona's theoretical properties including finite-sample coverage and, in the noiseless case, convergence to the true state and derivatives under dense sampling. In a nonlinear regression benchmark on six functions of three to eight dimensions, Diona was more accurate than a Gaussian process (GP) on noiseless data especially with denser data sets. Furthermore, as with GP, it produced uncertainty bounds that contained the true value at more than 95% of query points in four functions. Diona's time to a first prediction after a data set update was three to four orders of magnitude shorter than that of the GP, and two to three orders shorter than that of a neural network, which was more accurate but offers no uncertainty quantification. This low latency is paid for by on-demand predictions, so this latency advantage applies when relatively few predictions are needed between data updates.

papers.title: Positive sectional curvature on exotic spheres in infinitely many dimensions
papers.abstract: We show that there exist exotic spheres with metrics of strictly positive sectional curvature in infinitely many dimensions: in every dimension $n\equiv3\pmod4$ with $n\geq11$ and $n\not\equiv255\pmod{256}$. Previously, every known closed simply connected manifold of positive sectional curvature in a dimension above $24$ was diffeomorphic to a compact rank-one symmetric space. The spheres we consider are certain homotopy spheres arising as quotients of special $S^3$-$S^3$ bundles introduced by Sperança. These homotopy spheres are determined by an orthogonal representation $ρ$ of $S^3$ and an $S^3$-conjugation-equivariant map $β$, and are denoted $Σ_{ρ,β}$. By recent constructions, such spheres admit Riemannian metrics of strictly positive sectional curvature. In this paper we consider the spheres $Σ_{ρ_b,β}$ of dimension $4b+3$, $b\geq2$, where $ρ_b$ is the representation of $S^3$ on $\mathbb{R}^3\oplus\mathbb{H}^b$ by left multiplication on the second summand. For these spheres, we show that the Eells-Kuiper invariant is the product of an integer $k(β)$ depending only on $β$ and a rational number $r_b$ given by one coefficient of a power series built from the $\hat A$- and $L$-genera. We then show that, for every $b\geq2$ with $b\not\equiv63\pmod{64}$, there is a map $β$ for which the Eells-Kuiper invariant does not vanish, and thus the corresponding sphere is exotic. A computer calculation also gives the dimensions $n\equiv255\pmod{256}$ below $2^{16}$.
papers.comments: 36 pages, 3 tables. Programs and outputs archived at Zenodo, doi:10.5281/zenodo.23571372

papers.title: Polytopal substitutions and conformal dimension
papers.abstract: We introduce polytopal substitutions, a recursive procedure for constructing polyhedral approximations of self-similar topological spaces. For a class of substitutions called sub-hyperbolic, we show that the limit of these approximations is naturally homeomorphic to the limit space of the associated iterated monodromy group. We establish a relationship between the $\ell^p$-contraction coefficients of sub-hyperbolic substitutions and the conformal dimension of their limit spaces. In particular, we characterize the conformal dimension in terms of asymptotic moduli and relate these moduli to $p$-energies of graphs.

papers.title: A spectral multiplier theorem for fractional Hardy operators
papers.abstract: We consider the fractional Laplacian with added critical or subcritical Hardy potential, called Hardy operator. We prove a Hörmander spectral multiplier theorem, i.e., the boundedness of sufficiently smooth multipliers of these Hardy operators on Lebesgue spaces. The range of admissible Lebesgue exponents is optimal, but the smoothness assumption is probably not. The proof combines the Helffer--Sjöstrand formula with a quantitative Jaffard lemma for operator-valued matrices.

papers.title: Triple Quantum Schubert Calculus
papers.abstract: We prove a triple quantum Pieri formula: the product of a quantum double Schubert polynomial $\widetilde{\mathfrak{S}}_u(x;y)$ by a quantum factorial elementary polynomial $\widetilde{E}_{p,k}(x;z)$ in a second set of variables $z$ is a sum over chains in the quantum Bruhat graph, indexed by a quantum analogue of Sottile's relation, whose coefficients are monomials in the quantum parameters times polynomials in the differences $y_i-z_j$ with nonnegative integer coefficients, and which is Graham-positive at $z=y$. At $y=z=0$ it is the quantum Pieri rule of Ciocan-Fontanine and Postnikov; at $z=y$ it is an equivariant quantum Pieri rule for the complete flag variety, indexed by chains in the quantum Bruhat graph rather than, as in the rule of Huang and Li, by the data of a reduction to classical cohomology, and proved directly. A doubled Pieri formula, positive in the same senses, treats multiplication by the quantization of a product of two elementary polynomials in the same variables, which is not the product of the quantizations: it is two iterated Pieri steps with the incompatible pairs of chains omitted. More generally, the triple quantum Schubert structure constants $c_{u,v}^{w,d}(y;z)$, the coefficients of $\widetilde{\mathfrak{S}}_u(x;y)\widetilde{\mathfrak{S}}_v(x;z)$ in the basis $\{\widetilde{\mathfrak{S}}_w(x;y)\}$, are polynomials in the $y_i-z_j$ with nonnegative integer coefficients; the proof of this appears as an appendix. We extend the Peterson-Woodward comparison formula and the quantum-to-classical reduction of Leung-Li and Huang-Li to the triple constants, and we describe and prove correct the algorithms of schubmult, which compute products of arbitrary quantum double Schubert polynomials well beyond the reach of previous methods.
papers.comments: 57 pages. Includes an appendix by Tongren Xiao and Yihua Yue proving triple quantum Schubert positivity. Algorithms implemented in the Python package schubmult

papers.title: Short curves in homogeneous spaces of the unitary group for unitarily invariant norms
papers.abstract: Let A be a unital *-subalgebra of $M_n(C)$ and let $M = U(n)/U(A)$, with the quotient Finsler metric induced by a unitarily invariant norm on $u(n)$, normalized so that $||iP|| = 1$ for rank-one projections $P$. This family contains the unitary orbits of Hermitian matrices, in particular flag manifolds and Grassmann manifolds. We prove that if $z_0$ is a minimal lifting of a tangent vector $X$ with $||X||_{\infty} < π/2$, then the one-parameter group $t \mapsto e^{t z_0}\cdot o$ has minimal length among all piecewise smooth curves in $M$ joining its endpoints. The same holds in manifolds $N=SU(n)/(SU(n) \cap A)$ for every Ad-invariant Finsler norm on $su(n)$, not necessarily symmetric (i.e. the unit sphere does not need to be balanced). The proof relies on the convexity of the distance from the identity along geodesic segments, valid for all these norms. We also prove that the ball of radius $π/2$ around the identity, for the spectral norm, is convex along one-parameter segments. This extends known results for the p-Schatten norms with p even, and gives a new proof for the operator norm, where the result is due to Duran, Mata-Lorenzo and Recht.

papers.title: Dispersive Tree Agreements for Multi-Robot Coordination
papers.abstract: Multi-robot coordination of nonlinear systems is naturally formulated as joint-space optimal control subject to constraints over groups of robots. Existing methods that approach joint optimality remain largely centralized, offline, and confined to collision-free motion planning, while decentralized, real-time counterparts target safe navigation without pursuing the joint optimum. This paper develops a decentralized, real-time planner that approaches the joint optimum as an anytime process. We extend a recent single-robot framework that searches dispersive trees of forward-propagated commands for differentially flat systems to coordinate a multi-robot team near-optimally. We first show that the inter-robot coupling can be effectively replaced by some local constraints, under which locally grown dispersive trees contain a near-optimal agreement. It is this structure that the robots pursue by decentralized column generation, negotiating rents on the shared space that guide the search of each robot's tree. The negotiation settles on an agreement whose near-optimality is certified at quiescence. Our protocol, WarpWeaver, implements this negotiation as an asynchronous real-time loop over a receding horizon, and demonstrates effective closure to quiesced agreements even when real-time deadlines cut the negotiation short. In simulation, WarpWeaver reduces total travel time by up to 22% against centralized offline planners on the Dynobench suite and by up to 37% against a decentralized real-time baseline, and nearly doubles the success rate of a task-specific planner on graph connectivity. Hardware experiments on six robots planning onboard demonstrate real-world implementability.
papers.comments: 19 pages, 5 figures, 7 tables. Submitted to IEEE Transactions on Robotics

papers.title: A sharpened $L^8_t L^4_x$-Strichartz estimate for even initial data
papers.abstract: It is well known that $u_0 \in L^2(\mathbb{R}) \setminus \{0\}$ is an extremizer for the $L^8_t L^4_x$-Strichartz estimate if and only if it is a Gaussian. We show that every extremizing sequence of even functions $\{ u_n \} \subset L^2(\mathbb{R}) \setminus \{0\}$ approaches a centered Gaussian in an appropriate sense. This result follows from a certain inequality for coordinate-wise even $L^2$ functions on $\mathbb{R}^4$ conjectured by Gonçalves (2019) which we prove in this paper with the optimal constant.

papers.title: Convex Bernstein limits and sharp recovery on expanding intervals
papers.abstract: We determine when approximation by convex polynomials on expanding intervals converges to best approximation on the real line by convex entire functions of exponential type at most $σ>0$. For intervals of radius $(n-γ_n)/σ$, where $0\leγ_n<n$ and $γ_n=o(n)$, one margin sequence gives this limit for every convex function of polynomial growth if and only if $γ_n/[n^{1/3}(\log n)^{2/3}]\to\infty$. When this condition fails, a fixed uniformly strictly convex entire function has approximation errors with unbounded limsup. We apply the limit theorem to prove existence of the convex Bernstein constant for $|x|^λ$ for every $λ\ge1$, and identify it with an attained entire-function minimum. We also give a sufficient margin for growth bounded by $\exp(a|x|^α)$, $0<α<1$. For arbitrary subexponential growth on the real line, each target with finite entire-function error admits a suitable margin, whereas no single margin is sufficient for the whole class. Further results concern attainment, right continuity with respect to the exponential type, weighted growth conditions, and the endpoints of fixed-fraction approximation intervals.

papers.title: Searching for the power rangers
papers.abstract: We develop a method for studying centralizers of generic elements in some large Polish groups. We identify a condition which enables us to show that the range of each power map is comeager; a strengthening of this condition allows us to prove that a generic element embeds in a flow (a continuous, one-parameter subgroup). This approach enables us to answer the question that motivated this work : we prove that a generic isometry of the Urysohn space (or the Urysohn sphere) embeds in a flow. We also obtain information on the centralizer of a generic isometry; we show that it contains an infinite-dimensional torus and that torsion elements are dense in it. To illustrate the flexibility of our method, we apply it to two other Polish groups. The first is the group of measure-preserving automorphisms of a standard probability space, and we recover results of King and of de la Rue and de Sam Lazaro. Finally we apply our technique to the group of nonsingular automorphisms of a standard probability space, and we deduce that a generic nonsingular automorphism embeds in a flow, answering a question of Danilenko and Silva.

papers.title: Bulk stability of bimolecular stochastic chemical reaction networks
papers.abstract: We establish criteria for stability in the bulk of planar stochastic chemical reaction networks with mass-action kinetics. Using Poincaré compactification, we characterize the asymptotic drift and show how stochastic fluctuations can prevent escape along transversally repulsive branches of the limiting deterministic flow. We construct a Lyapunov function by combining local estimates near these branches with dissipative estimates in the neighboring regions. The criteria cover a wide class of networks and in particular apply beyond weakly reversible and strongly endotactic networks. Together with compatible boundary estimates, these criteria imply positive recurrence.

papers.title: Lipschitz clustering in normed spaces and barycentric spaces
papers.abstract: For every normed space $X$ and integers $1\le k<n$, we construct a Lipschitz retraction from $X(n)$ onto $X(k)$ with constant at most $2+8n(n-1)$, independently of the dimension of $X$. Here $X(n)$ consists of the nonempty subsets of $X$ with at most $n$ points, equipped with the Hausdorff metric. For the consecutive case $k=n-1$, a separate construction gives the sharper asymptotic bound $O(n\log n)$. These results extend to barycentric metric spaces and settle some open problems on Lipschitz retractions.

papers.title: The generic splitting type of the logarithmic bundle of an arrangement of at most sixteen lines is combinatorial
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an arrangement of $d$ lines in $\mathbb{P}^2_\mathbb{C}$ and let $\mathcal{T}\langle\mathcal{A}\rangle$ be its bundle of logarithmic vector fields. On a general line, $\mathcal{T}\langle\mathcal{A}\rangle$ splits as $\mathcal{O}(-k)\oplus\mathcal{O}(k+1-d)$ with $k=\min\{\mathrm{mdr}(\mathcal{A}),\lfloor\frac{d-1}{2}\rfloor\}$, where $\mathrm{mdr}$ is the minimal degree of a Jacobian syzygy. We prove that $k$ is determined by the intersection lattice whenever $d\le16$, answering in this range a question of Cook, Harbourne, Migliore and Nagel. Since freeness can be read off from $k$ and $c_2(\mathcal{T}\langle\mathcal{A}\rangle)$, this strengthens Terao's freeness conjecture in this range; in particular we obtain a proof of Terao's conjecture for $14$ lines that uses it only for $13$ lines. For any number $d$ of lines, it follows that $\mathrm{mdr}$ is determined by the lattice whenever $\mathrm{mdr}\le6$ and $2\mathrm{mdr}\le d-3$, and that Terao's conjecture holds for every free arrangement whose smaller exponent is at most $7$. The proof reduces the question to critical arrangements: $2s+3$ lines, each containing at most $s+1$ intersection points, with $\mathrm{mdr}=s$. For these, the inflection polynomial of the minimal derivation factors as $Q_\mathcal{A} R$ with $R\in H^0(\mathcal{I}_Z^2(s-3))$, where $Z$ is the zero scheme of the derivation, of length $ν=c_2(\mathcal{T}\langle\mathcal{A}\rangle)-s(s+2)$. For $s\le5$ this forces $ν\le1$, and Chern class arguments then reduce everything to Terao's conjecture for $13$ lines. For $s=6$ we show $ν\le3$, using a Riccati equation along multiple components of $R$, Ziegler's multirestriction, and local computations verified by computer algebra; an exhaustive enumeration of the 26,265,318 candidate lattices with $ν\in\{2,3\}$ that satisfy Bojanowski's inequality completes the proof.
papers.comments: 26 pages, 1 table. Theorem B is computer-assisted; the programs, the screening logs, the realizable classes and checksums of the enumeration output are in the ancillary files

papers.title: The domination number of the 2-token graph of the complete bipartite graph
papers.abstract: For a graph $G$, the $2$-token graph $F_2(G)$ has as vertices all $2$-subsets of $V(G)$, with two such subsets adjacent whenever their symmetric difference is an edge of $G$. In this paper, we determine the domination number of the $2$-token graph of the complete bipartite graph $K_{m,n}$, for all integers $2\le m\le n$. We show that it equals $\lceil m/2\rceil+n-1$, except when $m=3$, or when $m\ge5$ is odd and $n=m+1$; in these two exceptional situations it is one less. Our arguments rely on an explicit characterization of the dominating sets of the $2$-token graph of $K_{m,n}$.
papers.comments: 14 pages, 3 Figures, 1 Table. Submitted for publication before the appearance of arXiv:2610.28936, whose results on F_2(K_{m,n}) were obtained independently. This version differs from the submitted one only by a footnote on arXiv:2610.28936 and three added references in the conclusions section

papers.title: Failure of noncommutative Rota's theorem with $L\log L$ endpoint
papers.abstract: We construct a factorizable Markov map $T$ on a hyperfinite finite von Neumann algebra and a positive element $x\in L\log L$ for which the sequence $T^n(T^*)^n x$ does not converge bilaterally almost uniformly. This answers a question of Anantharaman-Delaroche \cite{AD2006}.

papers.title: Boltzmann Equation and Hard Sphere Gas with Singular Initial Data: Well-posedness, Kinetic Limit, and Weak Stability
papers.abstract: We develop a local well-posedness theory for the spatially inhomogeneous 3-d Boltzmann equation with hard sphere cross-section, accommodating a class of large initial data. This class is an interpolation between the space $L_{x}^{\infty}L_v^{1}$ and $L_{v}^1L_{x}^{\infty}$ (with weight in $v$). It is notable for including data that can have infinite $L_{x,v}^\infty$-norm, entropy density. The core idea of the proof is a homogenization method based on collision geometries. As a key application, we prove the kinetic limit of hard sphere gases with initial data in this space, having certain extra conditions. This is the first proof on the kinetic limit of hard sphere gases with singular initial data. We also derive weak stability estimates of Boltzmann equation and hard sphere gas within the same functional spaces.

papers.title: A Sharp Gradient Harnack Estimate for the Lane--Emden System
papers.abstract: We establish a sharp pointwise gradient estimate for positive entire classical solutions of the Lane--Emden system when one of the exponents lies below the Serrin exponent $n/(n-2)$. The estimate generalizes the positivity of the scalar curvature of the associated conformal metric in the biharmonic case $q=1$. The coefficient in the estimate is optimal on the critical hyperbola.

papers.title: Conway's thrackle conjecture: a new upper bound of $\frac43n$
papers.abstract: A thrackle is a drawing of a graph in the plane in which every pair of edges meets exactly once, either at a common endpoint or at a proper crossing. Conway conjectured that every thrackle has at most as many edges as vertices. We prove that every thrackle on $n\ge4$ vertices has at most $\left\lfloor4(n-1)/3\right\rfloor$ edges. The proof combines Pammer's computer-assisted verification of the conjecture for graphs on at most twelve vertices with a discharging argument in suitable plane and projective-plane embeddings.

papers.title: Upper tail large deviations of regular subgraph counts in sparse random regular graphs
